When the Egyptians cry out to the LORD under their oppressors, he will send them someone to save them, a champion who will set them free. 21The LORD will reveal himself to Egypt, and on that day Egypt will know the LORD. They will bring him sacrifices and grain offerings in worship; they will make vows to the LORD and fulfill them. 22The LORD will strike Egypt, striking and then healing. They will turn back to the LORD, and he will listen to their prayers and heal them. 23On that day a raised road will link Egypt with Assyria. Assyria will travel into Egypt, and Egypt into Assyria, and Egypt will join Assyria in worship.

A blessing in the middle of the earth

24On that day Israel will make a third with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the middle of the earth, 25whom the LORD of Armies has blessed with these words: “May Egypt, my people, be blessed, and Assyria, which my hands have made, and Israel, my own inheritance.”
fields.summary: In an oracle against Egypt, its rivers dry up and its counselors fail. Egypt will come to know God, and Egypt, Assyria and Israel will be a blessing in the middle of the earth.

fields.title: Isaiah 20
fields.body_html:
Naked and barefoot as a sign

1In the year that the commander-in-chief came to Ashdod, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, and fought against Ashdod and captured it, 2at that time the LORD spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz: “Go, untie the sackcloth from around your waist, and pull the sandals off your feet.” He did as he was told, walking about naked and barefoot.

3Then the LORD said, “My servant Isaiah has walked about naked and barefoot for three years, a sign and a forewarning against Egypt and Cush. 4In the same way the king of Assyria will drive off Egypt’s captives and Cush’s exiles, young and old, naked and barefoot, with their buttocks uncovered, the disgrace of Egypt. 5Then they will be shattered and disgraced, because Cush was their hope and Egypt their pride. 6On that day those who live along this coast will say, ‘Look at the fate of the ones we put our hope in, the ones we ran to for help, to save us from the king of Assyria! So how are we to escape?’”
fields.summary: Isaiah goes naked and barefoot for three years as a sign that Assyria will lead Egypt and Cush away captive.

fields.title: Isaiah 21
fields.body_html:
Babylon has fallen

1An oracle about the wilderness of the sea.
As storms tear across the Negev,
so it comes out of the desert,
from a land that strikes fear.
2A grim vision has been made known to me:
the betrayer still betrays, and the destroyer still destroys.
Advance, Elam! Besiege, Media!
I am ending all its groaning.
3That is why my body is racked with anguish;
pains have gripped me like the pains of a woman in labor.
What I hear bends me double;
what I see fills me with dread.
4My mind reels;
horror has overcome me.
The dusk I yearned for has been turned into dread for me.
5The table is laid, the carpets spread out; there is eating and drinking.
Get up, you officers! Rub oil on your shields!

6For the Lord said this to me:
Go and set up a lookout; whatever he sees, he must make known.
7When he sees a troop of riders, horsemen two by two,
men mounted on donkeys, men mounted on camels,
he must listen hard, with all his attention.
8Then he cried out like a lion,
“My lord, on the watchtower I stand without a break all day long,
and at my post I keep my place night after night.”
9And look, here it comes: a troop of men, horsemen two by two.
Then he spoke up, “She has fallen, Babylon has fallen!
Every carved image of her gods is smashed and thrown to the ground.”
10O my people, threshed like grain, crushed on my threshing floor!
What I heard from the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, I have announced to you.

Watchman, how far gone is the night?

11An oracle about Dumah.
Someone calls out to me from Seir,
“Watchman, how far gone is the night?
Watchman, how far gone is the night?”
12The watchman answers, “Morning is on its way, and night as well.
If you want to ask, then ask. Turn and come once more.”

An oracle about Arabia

13An oracle about Arabia.
You will spend the night in the scrubland of Arabia,
you caravans of Dedan.
14You who live in the land of Tema,
carry water out to the thirsty;
greet the fugitive with food for him.
15For they have fled before swords,
before the unsheathed sword, before the bow drawn taut,
before the heavy press of war.

16For the Lord said this to me: In one more year, counted as exactly as a hired worker counts his years, Kedar’s glory will all be gone. 17Of Kedar’s warriors, only a handful of bowmen will remain, for the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.
fields.summary: A watchman announces that Babylon has fallen. Oracles follow concerning Dumah and Arabia.

fields.title: Isaiah 22
fields.body_html:
The valley of vision

1An oracle about the valley of vision.
What is wrong with you now,
that all of you have climbed up onto the roofs?
2You are full of shouting, a city in uproar, a town in high spirits.
Your dead were not cut down by the sword or killed in battle.
3All your leaders ran away together and were taken prisoner without a bow being drawn.
All of you who were found were captured together, though they had fled far away.
4So I said, “Turn your eyes away from me; leave me to my bitter weeping.
Do not rush to comfort me
for the ruin of the daughter of my people.”
5For the Lord GOD of Armies brings a day of panic and trampling and confusion to the valley of vision,
a day when walls are broken through and cries ring out toward the mountain.
6Elam shouldered its quiver, with chariots, men and horsemen,
and Kir stripped the cover from its shield.
7Your finest valleys were filled with chariots,
and horsemen took up their stations at the gates.
8Judah’s covering was torn off,
and on that day you turned your eyes to the weapons in the House of the Forest.
9You saw how many breaches there were in the city of David,
and you gathered in the water of the lower pool.
10You numbered the houses of Jerusalem
and broke some of them down to make the wall stronger.
11Between the two walls you made a basin to hold the water of the old pool.
But you never looked to its maker,
or paid heed to the one who formed it long ago.
12On that day the Lord GOD of Armies called
for weeping and lament,
for shaved heads and for the wearing of sackcloth.
13Instead, there was feasting and merriment, cattle killed and sheep butchered,
meat eaten and wine poured.
“Let us eat and drink,” you said, “because tomorrow we will die!”
14The LORD of Armies has made himself known to my ears:
This guilt of yours will never be atoned for until the day you die,
says the Lord GOD of Armies.

Shebna and Eliakim

15The Lord GOD of Armies says this:
“Go to this steward,
to Shebna, who is in charge of the palace, and say to him,
16‘What right do you have here, and who are your relatives here,
that you have hewn a tomb for yourself here?
He carves his grave high on the hill
and hollows out a home for himself in the rock!
17Look out, you strong man!
The LORD is going to fling you far away
and grip you hard.
18He will wind you round and round and fling you like a ball
into a broad, open country.
There you will die, and there your splendid chariots will stay,
you disgrace to your master’s house!
19I will drive you out of your office,
and he will pull you down from your post.
20When that day comes, I will call for my servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah. 21I will dress him in your robe and bind your sash on him. I will place your authority in his hand, and he will be a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. 22I will lay the key of the house of David on his shoulder. When he opens, no one will close; when he closes, no one will open. 23I will drive him in like a peg where the ground holds fast, and he will be a seat of honor for his father’s house. 24They will hang on him the whole weight of his father’s family, its children and its descendants, every small vessel, from basins to every storage jar. 25On that day, declares the LORD of Armies, the peg fixed in a secure place will work loose. It will be hacked off and fall, and everything it held will be cut away, for the LORD has spoken.’”
fields.summary: Jerusalem feasts when it should mourn, trusting its defenses instead of God. Shebna the steward is removed, and Eliakim is given the key of the house of David.

fields.title: Isaiah 23
fields.body_html:
The oracle concerning Tyre

1The oracle concerning Tyre.
Wail, ships of Tarshish! Tyre lies in ruins, with no house left standing and no port to come home to.
From the land of Kittim the news has reached them.
2Be still, you people of the coast,
whom Sidon’s traders filled with wealth as they sailed the sea.
3The grain of Shihor crossed the mighty waters;
what the Nile harvested brought her income,
and she grew into a market for the nations.
4Hang your head in shame, Sidon,
because the sea, the sea’s stronghold, cries out:
“I have known no labor pains and borne no children; I have raised no young men and brought up no young women.”
5When the news reaches Egypt,
they will shake with pain at what they hear of Tyre.
6Sail away to Tarshish!
Wail, you who live on the coast!
7Is this your rejoicing city,
whose story began in ancient days? Her own feet took her far away to make her home among strangers.
8Who made this plan against Tyre, which once handed out crowns?
Her traders ranked as princes;
her merchants were honored across the earth.
9The LORD of Armies planned it,
to stain the pride that every splendor brings
and to bring low all the earth’s honored ones.
10Spread over your land as the Nile spreads,
Daughter Tarshish; nothing holds you in any longer.
11He has reached out his hand over the sea
and set kingdoms trembling.
The LORD has issued orders against Canaan,
that her fortresses be torn down.
12He said: You will celebrate no more,
you ravaged virgin, Daughter Sidon. Get up, cross over to Kittim;
even there no rest awaits you.
13See the land of the Chaldeans, a people who no longer exist!
Assyria gave it over to the beasts of the wilderness.
Its siege towers went up, its palaces were torn bare,
and it was left a heap of rubble.
14Wail, ships of Tarshish,
for your fortress has been laid waste!

Tyre forgotten for seventy years

15On that day Tyre will drop out of memory for seventy years, as long as one king’s lifetime. At the close of those seventy years, Tyre’s story will be like the prostitute’s song:
16“Pick up a harp and walk through the city, you prostitute whom everyone forgot!
Play sweetly, sing song after song,
so that someone will remember you.”
17At the end of the seventy years the LORD will turn his attention to Tyre. She will go back to earning her fee, selling herself to every kingdom of the world across the face of the earth. 18Yet what she gains and what she is paid will be holy, belonging to the LORD. No one will lock it away or pile it up. Her earnings will go to those who live in the presence of the LORD, to give them all the food they want and splendid clothing.
fields.summary: Isaiah’s oracle announces the fall of Tyre, which will be forgotten for seventy years and then restored.

fields.title: Isaiah 24
fields.body_html:
The earth laid waste

1Look! The LORD is about to strip the earth bare and lay it waste;
he will wrench its face out of shape and scatter the people who live on it.
2It will go the same for people and priest,
for servant and master, for maid and mistress,
for buyer and seller, for lender and borrower,
for the one who collects a debt and the one who owes it.
3The earth will be stripped completely bare and looted through and through,
for this is the word the LORD has spoken.
4The earth dries up and wilts;
the world shrivels and wilts;
the proudest of the earth’s people waste away.
5The earth lies polluted beneath the people who live on it,
for they have stepped over the instructions, brushed past the decree, and broken the covenant that was to last forever.
6That is why a curse eats away the earth,
and those who live on it pay for their guilt.
That is why the earth’s inhabitants are scorched away,
and only a handful of human beings remain.
7The new wine fails, the vine droops,
and all whose hearts were merry now groan.
8The merry beat of the tambourines is over,
the din of the revelers has stopped,
the gladness of the lyre is over.
9They no longer drink their wine to the sound of song;
beer turns bitter in the drinker’s mouth.
10The town of chaos is smashed;
every house is shut, and no one can get in.
11In the streets there is crying out over the wine;
all gladness has darkened into evening;
the joy of the earth has been carried off into exile.
12Only desolation is left in the city,
and the gate is smashed to rubble.
13For this is how it will be in the heart of the earth, among the peoples:
like an olive tree after it has been beaten,
like the last grapes picked once the harvest is over.
14These raise their voices and ring out with joy;
from the west they shout aloud at the majesty of the LORD.
15So honor the LORD in the lands of the dawn;
in the coastlands of the sea, honor the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

Songs from the edge of the earth

16From the edge of the earth we have heard songs: “Splendor belongs to the righteous one!”
But I said, “I am wasting away, wasting away! Woe to me!
The faithless keep breaking faith;
with faithless deeds the faithless break faith.”
17Fear and the pit and the trap
are upon you who live on the earth!
18Anyone who runs from the sound of fear will drop into the pit,
and anyone who climbs up out of the pit will be caught in the trap.
For the windows on high have been thrown open,
and the foundations of the earth quake.
19The earth is shattered to pieces;
the earth is torn right through;
the earth reels and shudders.
20The earth will lurch to and fro like a drunk;
it will rock like a watchman’s shelter.
Its rebellion will weigh it down;
it will fall and not get up again.

The LORD will reign on Mount Zion

21On that day the LORD will call to account the army of the heights up on high
and the kings of the earth down on the earth.
22They will be rounded up as prisoners are, into a pit,
and locked away in a prison;
after many days they will be brought to judgment.
23The moon will blush and the sun will hang its head,
for the LORD of Armies will reign as king on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem,
and before his elders there will be glory.
fields.summary: God will lay waste the earth because its people have broken the everlasting covenant. Songs rise from the edge of the earth, and God will reign on Mount Zion.

fields.title: Isaiah 25
fields.body_html:
Praise for the fall of the proud city

1LORD, you are my God!
I will lift you high and give thanks to your name.
You have worked a marvel:
purposes formed long ago, carried out with steadfast faithfulness.
2You have reduced a city to a mound of stones
and a walled town to rubble.
The palace-fort of foreigners has stopped being a city;
no one will ever build it again.
3So a mighty people will give you glory;
the city of brutal nations will stand in awe of you.
4You have been a fortress for the weak, a fortress for the needy when trouble pressed on them,
cover from the downpour and shade from the scorching sun.
The blast of tyrants is like a storm battering a wall.
5As heat bakes parched ground, so you bring down the roar of foreigners;
the way a passing cloud’s shade takes the edge off the heat, the tyrants’ song of triumph dies away.

A feast for all peoples on the mountain

6On this mountain the LORD of Armies will spread a banquet for all the peoples:
a feast of the richest food, a feast of wine long aged,
dishes rich with marrow, old wine strained clear.
7On this mountain he will swallow up the veil drawn over the faces of all the peoples,
the cloth woven across all the nations.
8He will swallow up death for all time.
The Lord GOD will wipe every face clean of tears
and lift from all the earth the disgrace of his people, for the LORD has spoken.

Waiting for God, and the fall of Moab

9On that day people will say:
Look, this is our God! We waited for him, and he will rescue us.
This is the LORD, the one we waited for;
let us be full of joy and delight in his salvation.
10The hand of the LORD will rest upon this mountain,
but Moab will be crushed underfoot on its own ground, like straw stamped down into a dung heap.
11There Moab will spread out its hands, as a swimmer spreads them out to swim,
but he will bring its pride down, for all the cunning of its hands.
12Your high fortress with its towering walls he will throw down; he will level it, bringing it to the ground, down into the dust.
fields.summary: The prophet praises God for the fall of the proud city. On the mountain God will prepare a feast for all peoples and swallow up death forever.

fields.title: Isaiah 26
fields.body_html:
The song of the strong city

1On that day they will sing this song in the land of Judah:
Ours is a mighty city;
he raises salvation around it for wall and rampart.
2Throw the gates wide,
so a righteous nation may march in, one that remains faithful.
3The mind that is held steady you guard in peace, unbroken peace,
for it relies on you.
4Put your trust in the LORD for all time,
for Yah, the LORD, is a rock that stands through every age.
5For he has humbled those who lived on the heights,
the city perched up high;
he brings it down, down to the ground,
and lays it level with the dust.
6It is trodden underfoot:
the afflicted walk over it, and the weak tread its ruins.
7For those who are righteous the road runs level;
Upright One, you smooth the track they walk.
8Even on the path where your judgments lead, LORD, we have waited for you;
our deepest longing is for your name, the name by which you are remembered.
9I long for you with all my being in the night,
and my spirit within me searches eagerly for you.
For whenever your judgments reach the earth,
the people of the world come to learn righteousness.
10Show mercy to the wicked, and still they will not learn righteousness;
even where all is upright they act crookedly,
blind to the majesty of the LORD.

A prayer for God to act

11LORD, your hand is lifted up, yet they take no notice.
They will see your burning devotion to your people, and shame will cover them;
the very fire that waits for your enemies will devour them.

12LORD, you will set peace in place for us;
indeed, whatever we have accomplished was your doing for us.
13LORD our God, masters other than you have lorded it over us,
but it is you alone, your name, that we call on.
14They are dead and will not live again;
they are with the dead and will not rise.
That is why you dealt with them, wiped them out,
and erased every memory of them.
15You have made the nation grow, LORD,
you have made the nation grow; you have shown your glory
and pushed out every border of the land.
16LORD, when hardship came they sought you out;
under your correction they poured out a hushed prayer.
17Like an expectant mother whose hour has come,
who twists in pain and cries out in her labor,
that is how we have been before you, LORD.
18We conceived and labored, but it was as if we bore only wind.
We have won no deliverance for the earth,
and no new inhabitants of the world have been born.
19Your dead will live; my dead bodies will rise.
Wake up and shout with gladness, you who lie in the dust! For your dew is a dew of shining light,
and the earth will bring the dead to birth.

Hidden until the wrath passes

20Come, my people, step inside your rooms and bar the doors behind you.
Keep hidden for a short while, until the wrath has gone past.
21Look! The LORD is setting out from his place
to call the people of the earth to account for their guilt.
The earth will lay bare the blood poured out on it
and no longer keep its slain covered.
fields.summary: Judah sings of its strong city and prays for God to act. God’s dead will live, and the people are to hide until God’s wrath has passed.

fields.title: Isaiah 27
fields.body_html:
The sword of the LORD against Leviathan

1On that day the LORD will take his great sword, harsh and strong, and bring it down on Leviathan the serpent in flight,
on Leviathan the coiling serpent;
he will kill the monster that lives in the sea.

A new song of the vineyard

2On that day,
sing of a vineyard of delight!
3I, the LORD, am the one who tends it.
I give it water moment by moment.
So that no one will do it harm,
I stand guard over it night and day.
4There is no anger in me.
If only thorns and briers stood against me in battle!
I would advance on them and burn them all at once.
5Or else let them take hold of me as their stronghold.
Let them make peace with me;
peace with me let them make.
6In the days ahead Jacob will put down roots;
Israel will flower and send out shoots,
and they will cover the face of the world with fruit.

7Has he struck Jacob the way he struck the one who struck him?
Or has Jacob been slain the way his slayers were slain?
8In due measure, by sending her away, you contended with her;
he swept her off with his fierce blast on the day the east wind blew.
9So by this Jacob’s guilt will be covered over,
and this is the full harvest that comes from taking his sin away:
he will make every altar stone like chalk crushed to powder,
and no Asherah pole or incense altar will be left standing.
10For the walled city sits alone,
a home left empty and abandoned like the desert.
Calves graze there; there they lie down and strip its branches bare.
11When its boughs dry out they snap off,
and women come and use them to light their fires.
For these people have no understanding.
So he who made them will feel no pity for them; he who shaped them will show them no kindness.

Gathered one by one

12On that day the LORD will beat out the grain from the current of the Euphrates down to the Wadi of Egypt, and you will be picked up one at a time, Israelites.

13On that day a great ram’s horn will sound. Those lost in the land of Assyria will come, with those driven off into the land of Egypt, and they will bow down to the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
fields.summary: God will punish Leviathan, and a new song is sung over the fruitful vineyard of Israel. The scattered people will be gathered one by one to worship in Jerusalem.

fields.title: Isaiah 28
fields.body_html:
A fading crown and a lasting one

1Woe to the proud garland of Ephraim’s drunkards,
to the wilting blossom of its splendid beauty,
set at the head of the fertile valley of those laid low by wine!
2Look, the Lord holds ready one who is mighty and powerful.
Like a storm of hail and a wrecking wind,
like a downpour of great waters that sweep all before them, he will dash it to the ground by force.
3The proud garland of Ephraim’s drunkards
will be trodden underfoot.
4And the wilting blossom of its splendid beauty, set at the head of the fertile valley,
will be like the first fig that ripens before summer:
someone catches sight of it,
and before it has left his hand, he has eaten it.

5On that day the LORD of Armies himself will be the splendid crown,
the beautiful garland,
worn by the survivors of his people,
6the spirit of justice
in the one who presides over the court,
and the strength of those who hurl the attack back at the gate.

Drunken priests and prophets

7Yet these too sway with wine
and lurch with beer.
Priest and prophet sway with beer and are swallowed up by wine. They lurch from beer,
sway as they see visions, and totter when they hand down a ruling.
8Every table is smeared with vomit; there is filth everywhere,
and no clean place.

9Who does he imagine he is teaching? Who needs his lessons explained?
Babies just off milk, newly taken from the breast?
10It is all tsav latsav, tsav latsav,
qav laqav, qav laqav,
a little here, a little there!
11Indeed, with halting speech and in a foreign language
he will speak to this people,
12to whom he once said, “Here is rest: give the weary rest. Here is relief.”
But they refused to hear it.
13So the word of the LORD will come to them as tsav latsav, tsav latsav, qav laqav, qav laqav,
a little here, a little there,
so that they will walk on and fall backward, broken,
trapped, and taken captive.

A covenant with death and a stone in Zion

14Now then, you men who sneer,
you who govern this people in Jerusalem: listen to what the LORD says!
15For you have said, “We have made a covenant with death;
we have a pact with Sheol.
When the flooding whip sweeps through, it will not reach us,
for we have taken shelter in a lie and hidden ourselves inside falsehood.”

16So the Lord GOD says this:
Look, I have laid a stone in Zion as its foundation:
a stone proven by testing, a valuable cornerstone, set deep and secure.
The one who trusts will not rush in panic.
17Justice will be my measuring line,
and righteousness my plumb line.
Hail will sweep away the shelter of lies,
and floodwaters will swamp the hiding place.
18Your covenant with death will be wiped out,
and your pact with Sheol will fail.
When the flooding whip sweeps through,
it will trample you into the ground.
19Each time it comes through, it will seize you.
It will come through every morning, by day and by night.
When at last you grasp the message, it will be only terror.
20The bed is too short for anyone to stretch out on it,
and the blanket too skimpy to wrap up in.
21As at Mount Perazim, the LORD will stand up;
as in the valley near Gibeon, he will burst into fury,
to do his deed, a strange deed,
and to carry out his work, an alien work.
22Now then, give up your scoffing,
or your chains will grip you harder.
For I have heard from the Lord GOD of Armies of an end, complete and decreed, coming upon the whole land.
23Turn your ear and hear my voice;
take note and listen to what I say.
24Does the farmer who plows to plant go on plowing all day long?
Does he never stop breaking open and harrowing his soil?
25Once he has made the ground level,
does he not scatter black cumin, sow cumin seed,
set wheat in rows, barley in its marked plot, and spelt along the border?
26His God has trained him in the proper order of things and teaches him.
27No one threshes black cumin with a sledge or rolls cart wheels over cumin.
Black cumin is knocked loose with a stick, and cumin with a rod.
28Grain for bread must be crushed, but no one keeps on threshing it endlessly.
He drives the wheels of his cart and his horses over it, but he does not grind it to dust.
29This too comes from the LORD of Armies,
whose counsel is a wonder and whose wisdom is great.
fields.summary: Woe to the fading crown of Ephraim and to drunken priests and prophets. Jerusalem’s rulers have made a covenant with death, but God lays a tested stone in Zion.

fields.title: Isaiah 29
fields.body_html:
Woe to Ariel

1Woe to Ariel, Ariel, the town where David made camp!
Add one year to another; let the festivals come around again.
2Then I will press Ariel hard;
there will be mourning and moaning,
and she will be to me like an altar hearth.
3I will camp in a ring all around you;
I will hem you in with siege posts
and set up siege works against you.
4Brought low, you will speak from the ground;
your words will come muffled from the dust.
Your voice will rise from the earth like a ghost’s,
and from the dust your words will chirp.
5Yet the horde of your foes will be like fine dust,
the horde of the ruthless like chaff that blows away.
It will happen in a moment, all at once.
6The LORD of Armies will come to her
with thunder, earthquake, and a mighty roar,
with gale and tempest and the blaze of a fire that consumes.
7Then the horde of all the nations that make war on Ariel,
all who attack her and her stronghold and press her hard,
will be like a dream, like something seen in the night.
8It will be like someone hungry who dreams of eating, then wakes and the stomach is still empty;
like someone thirsty who dreams of drinking, then wakes weak, the throat dry and craving.
That is how it will be for the horde of all the nations that make war on Mount Zion.

Blind eyes and a sealed scroll

9Go slow and stand stunned; make yourselves blind and stay blind!
They are drunk, though not with wine;
they reel, though not from strong drink.
10The LORD has poured over you a spirit of heavy sleep.
He has shut your eyes, that is, your prophets;
he has wrapped your heads, that is, your seers.
11This whole vision has become for you like the words of a sealed scroll. People hand it to someone who can read and say, “Please read this,” and the answer comes, “I cannot; it is sealed.” 12Or the scroll is handed to someone who cannot read, with the words, “Please read this,” and the answer comes, “I do not know how to read.”

13The Lord said: Since this people approaches me with words of the mouth
and gives me honor with their lips
while keeping their heart far from me,
and the fear they show me is only a human rule learned by rote,
14therefore I will once again deal with this people in astonishing ways, marvel after marvel.
The wisdom of their wise will come to nothing,
and the insight of their discerning will disappear from sight.

The potter and the clay

15Woe to those who burrow deep to keep their schemes hidden from the LORD!
Their deeds are done in a dark place,
and they say, “Who sees us? Who knows about us?”
16How you turn everything on its head!
Is the potter to be counted the same as the clay?
Should the thing that was made say of its maker, “He did not make me”?
Should the vessel say of the one who shaped it, “He has no sense”?
17Is it not only a little while longer before Lebanon becomes orchard land,
and the orchard land is counted a forest?
18On that day the deaf will hear the words written in a scroll,
and blind eyes will see, out of the gloom and the dark.
19The humble will have more and more joy in the LORD,
and the neediest of humankind will be glad in the Holy One of Israel.
20For the ruthless will be gone and the scoffer finished,
and all who are on the watch for a chance to do wrong will be cut off,
21those who make a person guilty with a single word,
who set snares for the one who speaks up for justice in the gate,
and with baseless claims turn the innocent away.

22Therefore the LORD, who redeemed Abraham, says this about the house of Jacob:
From now on Jacob will not be disgraced;
his face will not turn pale anymore.
23For when Jacob sees his children around him, children my hands have made, they will keep my name holy.
They will honor the Holy One of Jacob as holy
and tremble with awe before the God of Israel.
24People whose spirits have strayed will gain insight,
and the grumblers will take teaching to heart.
fields.summary: Woe to Ariel, Jerusalem, which will be besieged. The people honor God with their lips while their hearts are far away, and they forget that the potter is not like the clay.

fields.title: Isaiah 30
fields.body_html:
A useless alliance with Egypt

1Woe to the rebellious children, declares the LORD,
who carry through a scheme that does not come from me,
who seal a pact with a drink offering when my Spirit has not led them,
piling up sin after sin,
2who head down to Egypt without seeking my word,
to find safety in Pharaoh’s fortress
and to hide in Egypt’s shade.
3But the safety Pharaoh offers will turn into your shame,
and hiding in Egypt’s shade into your disgrace.
4His officials have gone as far as Zoan,
and his envoys have arrived at Hanes.
5But all of them will be humiliated by a nation that is of no use to them.
Egypt gives no help, no gain, nothing but shame and scorn.

6An oracle about the animals of the Negev.
Through a land of misery and hardship, where lioness and lion roam, and viper and flying serpent,
they load their wealth onto young donkeys and strap their treasures to the humps of camels,
bringing them to a people who can do them no good.
7Egypt’s help is mere breath, utterly empty.
So I have given her a name: Rahab, who sits and does nothing.
8Go now and write it on a tablet in front of them; set it down in a scroll,
so that it will last into the future, for all time to come.
9For they are a defiant people, children who deal falsely,
children who refuse to listen to the instruction of the LORD,
10who say to the seers, “Do not look,”
and to those who see visions, “Do not show us what is right.
Flatter us; dream up delusions.
11Get out of the way; step off the path;
take the Holy One of Israel out of our sight.”

12So the Holy One of Israel says this:
Since you have thrown aside this word,
and put your confidence in oppression and deceit, and lean on them,
13therefore this guilt will be for you like a split in a tall wall,
swelling outward and ready to fall,
until it gives way all at once, without warning.
14It will burst apart like a potter’s jar, smashed without mercy,
until not one piece is left large enough to lift coals from the hearth
or dip a little water out of a pool.

15For the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, says this: Come back and be at rest, and you will be rescued.
Your strength lies in staying calm and trusting.
But you would not.
16Instead you said, “No! We will race away on horses.” So race away you will!
“We will ride swift steeds.” So your pursuers will be swifter.
17A thousand of you will scatter at one man’s war cry; at the cry of five you will all scatter,
until what remains of you is like a bare pole on a mountaintop,
a lone flag on a hill.
18Even so, the LORD is waiting to be kind to you;
he is rising to have mercy on you.
For the LORD is a God of justice.
Those who wait for him are truly blessed.

Grace for the people of Zion

19A people will live in Zion, in Jerusalem,
and you will never weep again. At the sound of your cry he will surely show you grace;
the moment he hears it, he will reply.
20Though the Lord gives you hardship as your bread and distress as your water,
your Teacher will not keep himself out of sight any longer;
your eyes will see your Teacher.
21And when you stray to the right or to the left,
a word will sound in your ears from behind you:
“This is the road; keep walking on it.”
22Then you will treat as unclean the silver that covers your carved idols
and the gold that sheathes your metal images.
You will throw them away like a cloth from a woman’s monthly flow
and say to them, “Get out!”
23Then he will water with rain the seed you plant in the soil,
and the bread from the land’s harvest will be rich and full.
On that day your herds will feed in open pastures.
24Even the oxen and donkeys that plow the soil will eat salted feed,
winnowed clean with shovel and pitchfork.
25Water will run in streams and channels down every tall mountain and every raised hill
on the day of the great slaughter, when the towers topple.
26The moonlight will be as bright as sunlight,
and sunlight will be seven times stronger, like seven days’ light in one,
on the day the LORD bandages the fractures of his people
and heals the wounds his blows left.

The LORD comes against Assyria

27Look! The name of the LORD is coming from far away,
his anger burning and the smoke rising thick and heavy.
His lips brim with fury;
his tongue is like a fire that devours.
28His breath is like a river in flood that rises neck-high.
It comes to shake the nations in a sieve that sifts them to nothing,
and to fit a bridle on the jaws of the peoples that steers them astray.
29But for you there will be singing, as on the night a holy feast begins,
and joy in your hearts, like pilgrims walking to the flute’s tune
on their way to the mountain of the LORD, the Rock of Israel.
30The LORD will make the splendor of his voice ring out, and he will show his arm as it falls,
with furious anger and a flame of fire that devours,
with bursting storm, driving rain, and hailstones.
31At the voice of the LORD Assyria will be shattered with dread,
as he strikes it with the rod.
32Each time the LORD brings the rod he has appointed down on Assyria,
tambourines and lyres will sound,
and he will do battle against them with a raised and swinging arm.
33For Topheth was laid out long ago, and it stands ready for the king too.
Its pyre is broad and deep, heaped with plenty of wood for the fire,
and the breath of the LORD will kindle it like a river of sulfur.
fields.summary: Woe to those who make an alliance with Egypt instead of trusting God, for in coming back and resting they would be rescued. God longs to be gracious to Zion and will come against Assyria.

fields.title: Isaiah 31
fields.body_html:
Horses from Egypt or the Holy One of Israel

1Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help!
They lean on horses;
they put their confidence in chariots, for there are many of them, and in cavalry, for it is very strong.
But they do not turn their eyes to the Holy One of Israel;
they do not inquire of the LORD.
2But he is wise as well: he brings disaster and does not withdraw what he has said.
He will rise up against the house of evildoers
and against those who come to the aid of wrongdoers.
3Egypt is human and not God;
its horses are flesh and not spirit.
The LORD will stretch out his hand: the one who gives help will stagger, the one who receives it will go down,
and both will be finished together.

The LORD comes down to Mount Zion

4For the LORD has said this to me: Think of a lion, a young lion, rumbling over its kill. A crowd of shepherds is called out against it,
yet their yelling does not scare it
and their uproar does not make it shrink back.
In the same way the LORD of Armies will come down to wage war on Mount Zion and on its hill.
5Like birds on the wing, the LORD of Armies will protect Jerusalem:
he will protect and rescue, he will pass over and deliver.
6Turn back, Israelites, to the one from whom they have gone so deep into rebellion.
7For on that day each of them will spurn their idols of silver and their idols of gold,
the sin your own hands have made for you.
8Assyria will fall by a sword that no man wields;
a sword that is not human will devour it.
It will run from the sword,
and its young men will be put to forced labor.
9Its rock will give way in terror,
its officers will be shaken at the sight of the signal flag,
declares the LORD, who keeps a fire in Zion
and a furnace in Jerusalem.
fields.summary: Woe to those who rely on horses from Egypt instead of the Holy One of Israel. God will come down to defend Mount Zion.

fields.title: Isaiah 32
fields.body_html:
A king who reigns for righteousness

1Look: a king will reign to bring righteousness,
and princes will govern to see justice done.
2Each of them will be a place to hide from the wind and a cover from the downpour,
like channels of water in parched ground,
like the shade of a great rock in a worn-out land.
3The eyes of the seeing will not be sealed over then,
and the ears of the hearing will be alert.
4The hasty mind will come to understand and know,
and stammering tongues will be quick to speak plainly.
5No longer will a fool be called noble,
nor a swindler be spoken of as honorable.
6For a fool talks foolishness, and his mind works at evil:
he behaves godlessly and says twisted things about the LORD,
he sends the hungry away still empty
and cuts off drink from the thirsty.
7As for the swindler, his tools are crooked;
he dreams up schemes to bring the poor to ruin with lying words,
even when the needy person pleads what is right.
8The noble, though, makes noble plans,
and on what is noble he takes his stand.

Women at ease, and the Spirit from on high

9Women living at ease, stand up and hear my voice;
daughters so sure of yourselves, listen to my words.
10In a year and some days you will be shaken, you women so sure of yourselves;
the vintage will come to nothing, the ingathering will never arrive.
11Tremble, you women at ease; shake, you who feel so secure!
Strip off your clothes, lay yourselves bare, and wrap sackcloth around your waists.
12Strike your breasts in mourning
over the delightful fields, over the vine that was so fruitful.
13On the soil of my people thornbushes and briers will grow,
yes, over all the happy homes of the reveling town.
14For the palace will be deserted, the bustling city left empty;
Ophel and the watchtower will be dens for ever,
a playground for wild donkeys and grazing land for flocks,
15until the Spirit from on high is poured out upon us,
and the wilderness turns into orchard land,
and the orchard land is reckoned a forest.
16Justice will make its home in the wilderness,
and righteousness will live on in the orchard land.
17What righteousness produces will be peace;
what righteousness brings about will be calm and confidence for ever.
18My people will live in a peaceful homeland,
in safe dwellings, in resting places free from care.
19Hail will fall as the forest comes crashing down,
and the city will be brought low, utterly low.
20How blessed are you who sow beside all the waters
and send ox and donkey out to roam free!
fields.summary: A king will reign in righteousness. The women at ease are warned, until the Spirit is poured out from on high and justice and peace fill the land.

fields.title: Isaiah 33
fields.body_html:
Woe to the destroyer

1Woe to you, destroyer, never yet destroyed yourself,
and you who deal falsely, though no one has dealt falsely with you!
Once your destroying is done, you will be destroyed;
once you finish your treachery, others will deal treacherously with you.

A prayer in a time of distress

2LORD, show us grace; we have waited for you.
Be their strong arm morning by morning,
and our salvation when trouble comes.
3At the roar of the uproar the peoples run;
when you rise up, the nations scatter.
4Your spoil is swept up as caterpillars strip a field;
like a swarm of locusts people rush upon it.
5The LORD is exalted, for he lives on high;
he will fill Zion with justice and righteousness.
6He will be the firm foundation of your times,
a rich store of salvation, of wisdom and knowledge;
the fear of the LORD is his treasure.

7Listen! Their brave warriors cry out in the streets;
the envoys sent for peace weep bitter tears.
8The highways lie empty; no traveler walks the road.
He has broken the treaty and scorned the cities; he has no regard for human life.
9The land dries up and wastes away; Lebanon is put to shame and withers.
Sharon is like the desert plain, and Bashan and Carmel drop their leaves.
10Now I will rise up, says the LORD;
now I will show myself high and mighty; now I will lift myself up.
11You are pregnant with chaff, and you give birth to straw;
your own breath is a fire that will burn you up.
12The peoples will be burned to lime,
like thorns that are cut and set on fire.

Who can live with the devouring fire?

13You who are far away, hear what I have done;
you who are near, acknowledge my strength.
14The sinners in Zion are terrified; the godless are gripped by trembling:
“Which of us can live as a guest beside the devouring fire?
Which of us can stay where the burning lasts forever?”
15Whoever lives by what is right and speaks honestly,
whoever turns down profit squeezed from others, whose hands shake off a bribe instead of grasping it,
whose ears are closed to talk of bloodshed,
and whose eyes are shut against gazing at evil,
16that one will make a home on the heights, with fortresses of rock for refuge,
with bread supplied and water that never fails.
17Your eyes will see a king in his splendor;
they will look on a land that stretches far away.
18Your mind will think back on the terror:
“Where is the clerk who counted? Where is the one who weighed out the tribute?
Where is the officer who counted the towers?”
19You will no longer see that fierce nation,
a people whose speech is too strange to follow, whose stammering tongue makes no sense to you.
20Look at Zion, the city where we keep our festivals!
Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a home at rest, a tent that will never be taken down. Its pegs will never be pulled up,
and not one of its ropes will snap.
21Instead, there the LORD in majesty will be ours,
a place of rivers and wide streams,
where no galley with oars will sail
and no mighty ship will pass through.
22For our judge is the LORD, our lawgiver is the LORD,
our king is the LORD; he himself will save us.
23Your ropes hang slack;
they cannot hold the mast firm in its socket or spread out the sail.
Then plunder will be shared out in heaps,
and even the lame will carry off spoil.
24No one who lives there will say, “I am sick”;
the people who dwell in it will have their guilt forgiven.
fields.summary: Woe to the destroyer. The people pray in distress, and those who walk righteously will see the king in his beauty.

fields.title: Isaiah 34
fields.body_html:
Judgment on the nations and on Edom

1Come close and listen, you nations;
pay attention, you peoples!
Let the earth hear, and everything in it,
the world and all that springs from it.
2For the LORD is angry with all the nations,
furious with all their armies.
He has doomed them to destruction and handed them over to be slaughtered.
3Their dead will be flung aside unburied;
the reek of their corpses will rise,
and the mountains will run with their blood.
4The whole host of the heavens will decay,
and the sky will be rolled up like a scroll.
All its host will wither away,
the way a leaf withers on the vine, or a fig shrivels on its tree.
5In the heavens my sword has drunk its fill;
see, now it swoops down on Edom,
on the people I have set apart for destruction, to judge them.
6The LORD has a sword, and it drips with blood and is greasy with fat,
with the blood of lambs and goats,
with the fat from the kidneys of rams.
For in Bozrah the LORD is holding a sacrifice,
a great slaughter across the land of Edom.
7Wild oxen will go down with them in the slaughter,
bullocks along with the strong bulls.
Their land will be drenched with blood,
their dust glistening with fat.
8For the LORD has a day of vengeance,
a year of repayment, to take up Zion’s case.
9Its streams will be changed into tar and its dust into sulfur;
the whole land will become tar that burns.
10Its fire will burn night and day without going out,
and its smoke will go up for all time.
Age after age it will be a wasteland;
never again will anyone pass through it.
11The desert owl and the hedgehog will take it over;
the eared owl and the raven will nest there.
Over it he will stretch the builder’s line of formlessness and hold the plumb stones of emptiness.
12Its nobles will find no kingdom there to proclaim,
and all its princes will be gone.
13Thorns will spring up in its palaces,
nettles and thistles in its walled towns.
Jackals will make it their den,
and ostriches will claim it as their yard.
14The wild beasts of the desert will gather with the hyenas,
and the wild goat will cry to its companion.
The night creature, too, will settle there and find somewhere to lie at rest.
15There the arrow snake will nest and lay its eggs;
it will hatch them and gather its brood in its shade.
There the kites will flock together, every one with its mate.
16Search the scroll of the LORD and read it through:
of all these, not one will be absent,
and none will go without its mate.
It is my own mouth that gave the order, and his Spirit has brought them together.
17He has cast lots to give them their share,
and with his own hand he has measured it out to them.
They will hold it as their own for all time and live there age after age.
fields.summary: God’s wrath is poured out on the nations, and Edom is made a desolate wasteland.

fields.title: Isaiah 35
fields.body_html:
The wilderness in flower

1Wilderness and thirsty land will be glad;
the barren plain will exult and break into flower like the crocus.
2Its blossoms will be everywhere; it will exult with gladness and glad cries.
It will receive the glory of Lebanon,
the splendor of Carmel and of Sharon.
They will see the LORD in his glory, our God in his splendor.

Your God is coming to save you

3Put strength into hands that hang limp;
steady the knees that buckle.
4Tell those whose hearts are racing,
“Take courage; do not be afraid!
Here is your God. Vengeance is coming, God’s own repayment;
he himself is coming, and he will save you.”
5Then eyes that were blind will be opened,
and ears that were deaf will be unsealed.
6Then the lame will spring like a deer,
and the tongue of the mute will cry out with joy.
For in the wilderness water will burst out,
and in the barren plain, streams.
7The shimmering sand will turn into a pond,
and parched ground into springs of water.
Where jackals once had their lairs and lay at rest,
grass will give way to reeds and papyrus.
8A raised road will run there, a highway, and it will be named the Way of Holiness.
No one unclean will travel on it;
it will be for those who walk the way, and fools will not stray onto it.
9There will be no lion on it;
no savage beast will set foot on it or be found there.
Along it the redeemed will walk.
10Those the LORD has ransomed will come back; they will enter Zion with glad shouts,
with joy that never ends resting on their heads.
Delight and gladness will catch up with them,
and grief and groaning will run away.
fields.summary: The wilderness will burst into flower, the blind will see and the lame leap, and the redeemed will return to Zion with singing.

fields.title: Isaiah 36
fields.body_html:
The Assyrian officer at the walls of Jerusalem

1In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria marched against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them. 2Then the king of Assyria sent the chief officer from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a large army. The officer took his stand by the water channel from the Upper Pool, on the road to the Fuller’s Field. 3Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, went out to him, together with Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder. 4Then the chief officer said to them, “Tell Hezekiah, ‘The great king, the king of Assyria, says this: What sort of confidence is this that you are trusting in? 5I tell you, your strategy and your strength for war are nothing but empty words. Who is it you are leaning on, that you have rebelled against me? 6Look, you are leaning on Egypt, this cracked reed you use for a staff. Anyone who puts weight on it will have it run into the hand and pierce it. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is to all who rely on him. 7Or if you tell me, “Our trust is in the LORD our God,” did Hezekiah not get rid of his high places and his altars? Did he not tell Judah and Jerusalem, “It is before this altar that you must bow down”? 8Come, then, place a bet with my master the king of Assyria. I will hand you two thousand horses, if you can supply men to ride them! 9Then how could you drive off a single governor, one of my master’s lowest officials? Yet you put your trust in Egypt to send chariots and horsemen! 10And was it apart from the LORD that I came up to ruin this land? It was the LORD who said to me, “Go up against this land and ruin it.”‘” 11Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the chief officer, “We beg you, use Aramaic when you talk with your servants, because we know it. Do not talk to us in the language of Judah while the people on the wall are listening.” 12But the chief officer replied, “Did my master send me to speak these words just to you and your master? No, they are for the men who sit on the wall, who are going to eat their own dung and drink their own urine along with you!” 13Then the chief officer stood and shouted in the language of Judah: “Listen to the words of the great king, the king of Assyria! 14The king says this: ‘Do not let Hezekiah fool you. He has no power to rescue you. 15And do not let Hezekiah lead you to rely on the LORD when he tells you, “The LORD is sure to rescue us. The king of Assyria will never be given this city.”‘ 16Do not listen to Hezekiah. The king of Assyria says this: ‘Come to terms with me and surrender to me. Then everyone may eat from their own vine and their own fig tree and drink water from their own cistern, 17until I come to move you to a country like your own, a country of grain and fresh wine, of bread and vineyards. 18Watch out, or Hezekiah will lead you astray by saying, “The LORD will rescue us.” Did any of the gods of the nations ever rescue its own land from the hand of the king of Assyria? 19Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Did they rescue Samaria from my hand? 20Among all the gods of these countries, which ones have rescued their land from my hand, that the LORD should rescue Jerusalem from me?’” 21They stayed silent and did not say a word in reply, for the king had given an order: “Do not answer him.” 22Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, went to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and reported to him what the chief officer had said.
fields.summary: Sennacherib invades Judah, and his chief officer stands at the walls of Jerusalem mocking Hezekiah’s trust in God.

fields.title: Isaiah 37
fields.body_html:
Hezekiah sends word to Isaiah

1As soon as King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, wrapped himself in sackcloth, and entered the house of the LORD. 2He sent Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and the senior priests, all clothed in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz. 3They said to him, “Hezekiah says this: Today is a day of distress, of rebuke and of disgrace. Children have reached the opening of the womb, and there is no strength to bring them to birth. 4Perhaps the LORD your God will hear what the chief officer said when his master the king of Assyria sent him to insult the living God, and will call him to account for the words the LORD your God has heard. Lift up a prayer, then, for the remnant that is still here.” 5So King Hezekiah’s officials came to Isaiah. 6Isaiah said to them, “Say to your master, ‘The LORD says this: Do not be frightened by what you have heard, the words with which the king of Assyria’s lackeys have reviled me. 7I am about to put a spirit in him: he will hear a rumor and go back to his own country, and in his own country I will make him fall by the sword.’” 8The chief officer went back and found the king of Assyria attacking Libnah, for he had heard that the king had left Lachish. 9Then the king heard that Tirhakah king of Cush was marching out to fight against him. When he heard this, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying, 10“Say this to Hezekiah king of Judah: ‘Do not let your God, the one you rely on, deceive you by saying, “Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.” 11You yourself have heard how the kings of Assyria dealt with all the lands, wiping them out. And you expect to escape? 12Did the gods of the nations my forefathers destroyed rescue them, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar? 13Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, or of Ivvah?’” 14Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it through. He went up to the house of the LORD and opened it out in the presence of the LORD. 15Then Hezekiah prayed to the LORD, 16“LORD of Armies, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim: you, and no one else, are God of every kingdom on earth. It was you who made the heavens and the earth. 17Turn your ear, LORD, and listen; open your eyes, LORD, and look. Hear every word Sennacherib has sent to insult the living God. 18It is true, LORD, that the kings of Assyria have laid waste all these lands and their territory, 19and have flung their gods into the fire. Those were never gods, only wood and stone shaped by human hands, so they could destroy them. 20So now, LORD our God, rescue us from his power, so that every kingdom on earth will know that you alone are the LORD.” 21Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah: “The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: Because you have prayed to me about Sennacherib king of Assyria,
22this is the word the LORD has spoken against him:
The virgin, Daughter Zion, looks down on you and laughs at you;
Daughter Jerusalem shakes her head at your back.
23Do you know whom you have mocked and reviled?
At whom did you shout,
at whom did you lift your haughty eyes? At the Holy One of Israel!
24Through your servants you have mocked the Lord.
You said, ‘With chariots past counting I have climbed the mountain heights, the far ridges of Lebanon.
I will fell its loftiest cedars and its finest junipers.
I will reach its farthest summit and its lush forest.
25I have dug wells and drunk their water,
and under the tread of my feet every stream of Egypt will run dry.’
26Have you not heard? I did this long ago;
in days of old I shaped it.
Now I have made it happen,
so that you turn walled cities into heaps of rubble.
27Their people were powerless,
terrified and put to shame.
They were like the plants of the open field and fresh green herbs,
like grass on a rooftop, like a field of young shoots before the grain stands tall.
28I know where you sit, when you go out and when you come in,
and how you storm against me.
29Since you rage against me
and your arrogance has come up to my ears,
I will set my hook in your nose and my bit between your lips,
and I will lead you back along the same road by which you came.
30Here is the sign for you:
this year you will live on grain that sprang up untended,
and next year on whatever comes up after it;
but in the third year, sow and harvest, plant vineyards and eat what they bear.
31Those of the house of Judah who escape and are left will once more put down roots below
and bear fruit above.
32For a remnant will go out from Jerusalem,
and from Mount Zion those who have escaped.
The burning zeal of the LORD of Armies will make this happen.

33Therefore the LORD says this about the king of Assyria:
He will never set foot in this city.
He will not fire a single arrow into it,
nor face it with a shield,
nor pile up an earthen ramp against its walls.
34The road that brought him here will take him back again.
This city he will not enter, declares the LORD.
35I will shield this city and rescue it,
for my own sake and for my servant David’s sake.”

The end of Sennacherib’s campaign

36The angel of the LORD then went out and struck down 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. At dawn, when people got up, they found them all lying dead. 37So Sennacherib king of Assyria struck camp and went away. He returned home and stayed in Nineveh. 38While he was bowing down in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer, his own sons, cut him down with the sword and fled to the land of Ararat. Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.
fields.summary: Hezekiah sends word to Isaiah and prays, and Isaiah answers that Assyria will not enter the city. An angel strikes the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib is killed at home.

fields.title: Isaiah 38
fields.body_html:
Hezekiah is sick and is given fifteen years

1In those days Hezekiah fell ill and was close to death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, “The LORD says this: Give final instructions to your household, for you are dying and will not live.” 2Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall and prayed to the LORD. 3He said, “Please, LORD, remember how I have lived before you faithfully and with an undivided heart, doing what is good in your sight.” And Hezekiah wept loudly.

4Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah: 5“Go and say to Hezekiah, ‘The LORD, the God of your ancestor David, says this: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Now I will add fifteen years to your days. 6I will rescue you and this city from the grasp of the king of Assyria, and I will shield this city. 7And this will be your sign from the LORD that the LORD will carry out what he has said: 8Look, I will make the shadow that the sun has brought down the steps of Ahaz turn back ten steps.’” Then the sun turned back ten steps on the steps down which it had gone.

What Hezekiah wrote after his recovery

9A writing by Hezekiah king of Judah, after he had been sick and had recovered from his illness:
10I said, “At the midpoint of my days I must go into the gates of Sheol;
I am robbed of the years that remain to me.”
11I said, “I will not see Yah, Yah, in the land of the living.
I will look on human beings no more, once I dwell with those whose life has ceased.”
12My dwelling is uprooted and taken from me, like the tent of a shepherd.
I have rolled up my life as a weaver rolls up cloth; he cuts me free from the threads of the loom.
Before day turns to night you put an end to me.
13I lay quiet until morning;
like a lion he crushes all my bones.
Before day turns to night you put an end to me.
14I chatter like a swift or a crane;
I coo and mourn like a dove.
My eyes fail as I gaze on high.
Lord, I am overwhelmed; be my guarantor!
15What am I to say? He spoke to me, and he carried it out.
I will go softly all my years because of the bitterness of my soul.
16Lord, these are the things people live by,
and my spirit draws its life from all of them.
Heal me, and let me live!
17Yes, my bitter, bitter pain turned out for my good.
Because you loved my life, you drew it back from the pit of ruin;
you have tossed all my sins behind your back.
18For Sheol does not give you thanks; death offers you no praise.
Those who sink into the pit cannot look to your faithfulness.
19It is the living, the living who thank you, as I am doing now.
A father teaches his children about your faithfulness.
20The LORD has come to save me!
So all the days of our life we will make music on my strings at the house of the LORD.
21Isaiah had told them, “Have someone bring a lump of pressed figs and spread it on the sore, and he will live.” 22And Hezekiah had asked, “What sign is there to show that I will go up to the house of the LORD?”
fields.summary: Hezekiah is sick and is given fifteen more years, with the shadow on the steps as a sign. He writes a song of thanks after his recovery.

fields.title: Isaiah 39
fields.body_html:
Messengers from Babylon and a warning

1About that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, the king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah. He had heard that Hezekiah had been ill and had regained his strength. 2Hezekiah welcomed them gladly and showed them his treasury: the silver and the gold, the spices and the fine oil, his whole armory, and everything to be found in his storehouses. In his palace and across his whole kingdom, there was nothing he did not let them see. 3Then the prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and asked him, “What did these men say? And where did they come from to visit you?” Hezekiah answered, “They came to me from a faraway country, from Babylon.” 4He asked, “What did they see in your palace?” Hezekiah replied, “They saw all that is in my palace. In my storerooms there is not a thing I failed to show them.” 5Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Listen to the word of the LORD of Armies: 6Look, a time is coming when all that is in your palace, everything your ancestors have laid up until today, will be hauled off to Babylon. Not one thing will remain, says the LORD. 7Some of your descendants, born of your own line, will be taken away, and they will serve as eunuchs in the palace of the Babylonian king.” 8Hezekiah answered Isaiah, “This word of the LORD that you have brought is good.” He was thinking, “At any rate there will be peace and stability as long as I live.”
fields.summary: Hezekiah shows his treasures to messengers from Babylon, and Isaiah warns that all will be carried off to Babylon.

fields.title: Isaiah 40
fields.body_html:
Comfort my people

1Bring comfort, bring comfort to my people,
says your God.
2Speak to the heart of Jerusalem and call out to her
that her time of forced labor is finished,
that the penalty for her guilt has been paid,
that she has received from the LORD’s hand double for all her sins.

3A voice calls out:
In the wilderness clear a road for the LORD;
across the desert plain lay a straight highway for our God.
4Every valley will rise
and every mountain and hill will sink;
the broken ground will be made flat,
and the rugged heights an open plain.
5The glory of the LORD will be unveiled,
and every human being will see it together,
for the LORD has spoken it with his own mouth.

6A voice says, “Call out.”
And someone answered, “What should I call out?”
Humankind is grass,
and all its loyalty is like a wildflower.
7The grass dries out and the flower droops
when the wind of the LORD blows across it;
yes, the people are mere grass.
8Grass dries out and flowers droop,
but the word of our God holds firm for all time.

9Climb a high mountain, Zion, you who carry good news.
Shout with all your strength, Jerusalem, you who carry good news.
Shout and do not be afraid.
Tell the towns of Judah, “Here is your God!”
10Look, the Lord GOD is coming in power,
and his arm will rule for him.
Look, he brings his prize with him;
what he has won goes ahead of him.
11Like a shepherd he will pasture his flock.
He will gather the lambs into his arm
and carry them close against his chest,
and he will lead the nursing ewes with care.

Who can measure God?

12Who has measured the seas in the cup of his hand, or marked off the sky with the stretch of his fingers?
Who has gathered the dust of the earth into a basket,
or set the mountains on a scale
and the hills on a pair of balances?
13Who has taken the measure of the Spirit of the LORD?
What adviser of his has ever taught him?
14Whom did he ever ask for advice, so as to gain insight?
Who trained him in the path of justice,
or taught him knowledge,
or pointed out to him the road to discernment?
15The nations are no more than a drop falling from a bucket;
they count as the dust left on a scale.
He lifts up the coastlands like fine powder.
16Lebanon would not supply enough wood for the fire,
nor its wild animals enough for a burnt offering.

17Set beside him, all the nations amount to nothing;
to him they count for less than nothing, for an empty void.
18Who, then, will you say God is like?
What figure could you line up beside him?
19An idol? A craftsman casts it,
a goldsmith plates it in gold
and refines silver for its chains.
20The one who cannot afford so rich an offering
chooses a block of wood that will not decay
and goes looking for a skilled carver
to mount an idol that will not tip over.
21Do you not know? Have you not heard?
Was it not announced to you at the very start?
Have you not grasped it since the earth’s foundations were laid?
22He is the one enthroned high over the earth’s round horizon,
and the people living on it look like grasshoppers.
He draws the sky out like a sheer cloth
and spreads it like a tent to dwell in.
23He turns high officials into nothing
and makes the earth’s judges like a formless void.
24Hardly have they been planted, hardly have they been sown,
hardly has their stem rooted in the soil,
when he breathes on them and they shrivel,
and a gale whirls them away like straw.

25Who will you set beside me, as though I had an equal?
says the Holy One.
26Look up high and see. Who created these?
It is he who marches out their ranks in full count
and summons every one by name.
So vast is his might, so great his strength,
that not one fails to appear.

Strength for those who wait for the LORD

27Why do you say, Jacob, and why do you insist, Israel,
“My path is hidden from the LORD,
and my God lets my case slip by”?
28Do you not know? Or have you not heard? The LORD is the God of all ages, the maker of the earth to its farthest edges.
He does not tire or wear out,
and his understanding is beyond all searching.
29He gives strength to the exhausted
and builds up the power of those who have none.
30Youths grow faint and run out of strength;
young men in their prime trip and go down.
31But those who wait for the LORD will take on fresh strength.
They will climb high on outspread wings like eagles.
They will run and not wear out;
they will walk and not tire.
fields.summary: God tells the prophet to comfort God’s people, for their hard service is over. No one can measure God, who gives strength to the weary, and those who wait for God will climb high on outspread wings like eagles.

fields.title: Isaiah 41
fields.body_html:
The LORD calls the nations to court

1Coastlands, be still and listen to me;
let the peoples find new strength.
Let them step forward and then speak.
Come, we will go to court together.
2Who has roused a man from the east,
one whom righteousness summons at every step?
He gives up nations to him and makes him master of kings.
His sword reduces them to dust;
his bow scatters them like chaff in the wind.
3He hunts them down and goes on safely,
by a road his feet had never walked.
4Who has worked and achieved this?
Who summoned the generations at the very start?
I, the LORD, am the first,
and with the last I am still he.
5The coastlands watched and grew afraid;
the ends of the earth began to shake.
They came near; they gathered.
6They lend one another a hand;
each says to the next, “Stay strong!”
7The woodworker cheers on the metalworker;
the one who flattens metal with the hammer urges on the one who pounds the anvil.
“The joint is sound,” he says of the soldering,
and he fixes the idol in place with nails so it will not topple.

Do not be afraid, Israel my servant

8But you, Israel, are my servant;
you, Jacob, are the one I have chosen,
the descendants of my friend Abraham.
9I grasped you and brought you from the ends of the earth;
from its remotest corners I summoned you.
I said to you, “You are my servant.
I have chosen you; I have not thrown you away.”
10Do not be afraid, for I am with you;
do not glance about in alarm, for I am your God.
I give you strength; yes, I bring you help;
yes, I hold you up with my right hand, the hand of my righteousness.
11Look! Everyone who burns with anger against you will be put to shame and disgraced.
Those who quarrel with you will come to nothing and be lost.
12You will look for those who quarrel with you, but you will not find them.
Those who go to war against you will be like nothing, like what does not exist.
13For I, the LORD your God, have hold of your right hand;
I am the one telling you, “Do not be afraid. I will help you myself.”

14Do not be afraid, Jacob, worm that you are, you small band of Israel!
I am the one who will help you, declares the LORD.
The Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer.
15See, I am making you into a threshing sledge, sharp and new, its teeth double-edged.
You will tread the mountains and pound them to bits;
you will turn the hills to chaff.
16You will winnow them; the wind will lift them away and the storm will scatter them far.
And you will be glad in the LORD;
you will take pride in the Holy One of Israel.

17The afflicted and the poor hunt for water and find none;
thirst has dried their tongues.
I, the LORD, will answer them;
I, Israel’s God, will never leave them.
18On the bare heights I will open up rivers,
and springs in the middle of the valleys.
I will make the wilderness a pool
and the dry land a place of flowing springs.
19In the wilderness I will plant cedar and acacia, myrtle and wild olive;
in the desert plain I will put the juniper, the elm and the box tree side by side.
20All this is so that people will see and know, will ponder and understand together,
that it was the hand of the LORD that did this,
and the Holy One of Israel who created it.

The gods on trial

21Bring your lawsuit forward, says the LORD;
produce your strongest proofs, says the King of Jacob.
22Let them step up and announce to us what will come about.
The earlier events, what were they? Explain them, so that we may weigh them and learn where they led.
Or else let us hear of what is coming.
23Announce what lies ahead in time to come, and we will know that you are gods.
Go on, act; bring good or bring harm,
so that we may stare in alarm and all see it together.
24Look at you! You came from nothing, and your work is worthless air.
Whoever chooses you becomes detestable.
25I have roused someone in the north, and he is on his way;
out of the sunrise he will call on my name.
He will march over governors as over mud,
the way a potter stamps down wet clay.
26Who made this known at the start, for us to recognize?
Who spoke of it in advance, so that we might say, “Correct”?
There was not one to tell it,
not one to announce it, not one who heard a word from you.
27I was first to say to Zion, “See, they are here!”
To Jerusalem I send a herald with good news.
28When I look, there is nobody.
Among these there is not one adviser,
no one I can question who can give me an answer.
29See, they are all a delusion;
what they do is nothing;
their cast images are wind and emptiness.
fields.summary: God calls the nations to court and tells Israel, God’s servant, not to be afraid. The idols are put on trial and shown to be nothing.

fields.title: Isaiah 42
fields.body_html:
A servant who brings justice to the nations

1Here is my servant; I hold him up.
He is my chosen one, and I am well pleased with him.
I have placed my Spirit on him,
and he will carry justice out to the nations.
2He will not shout or make an uproar;
he will not send his voice ringing through the streets.
3He will not snap off a split reed
or smother a wick that is barely burning;
with faithfulness he will bring justice out.
4He will not burn low or be crushed
until he has set justice in place on the earth,
and the coastlands will wait in hope for his instruction.

5God, the LORD, says this, the one who created the heavens and stretched them out,
who hammered the earth flat and brought forth its growth,
who gives breath to the people living on it
and life to those who walk there:
6I, the LORD, called you for a righteous purpose; I will grip your hand and guard you.
I will make you a covenant for the people and a light for the nations,
7to give sight to blind eyes,
to lead captives out of their cells,
and out of the prison house those who sit in darkness.
8I am the LORD; that is my name.
My glory I will not hand over to anyone else,
nor the praise due to me to carved images.
9Look, what was foretold long ago has come about,
and now I announce things that are new.
Before they begin to sprout, I let you hear of them.

A new song from the ends of the earth

10Sing the LORD a new song;
let his praise sound from the far edge of the earth,
you seafarers and everything that fills the sea,
you coastlands and all who dwell on them.
11Let the desert and its towns lift their voices,
the camps where Kedar’s people live;
let those who live in Sela ring out with joy,
calling out from the peaks of the mountains.
12Let them bring glory to the LORD
and spread his praise through the coastlands.
13The LORD will go out like a hero;
like a seasoned soldier he will fire up his zeal.
He will shout, yes, raise the battle roar,
and prove his strength against his enemies.

14Long have I been silent;
I have kept still and held myself in check.
Now I will groan like a woman giving birth,
gasping and panting at once.
15I will strip mountains and hills bare
and parch every green thing on them.
I will turn rivers into dry land
and leave the marsh pools dry.
16I will lead the blind on a road strange to them
and guide them along tracks they have never walked.
Ahead of them I will change darkness to light and rough ground to level.
This is what I will do; I will not abandon them.
17But those who rely on a carved idol
and say to a cast image, “You are our gods,”
will be forced to retreat, covered with shame.

A servant who will not see or hear

18You deaf ones, listen!
You blind ones, look up and see!
19Who is so blind as my servant,
so deaf as the messenger I am sending?
Who is as blind as the dedicated one,
as blind as the servant of the LORD?
20You see so much, yet you take no notice;
his ears are open, yet he hears nothing.
21For the sake of his own righteousness, the LORD was glad
to make the instruction great and splendid.
22Yet they are a people robbed and stripped,
every one of them snared in holes
and locked away in jails.
They have become prey with none to rescue,
booty with none to say, “Return them!”
23Which one of you will open your ears to this,
attend closely, and listen from now on?
24Who gave Jacob up as spoil and Israel to raiders? Was it not the LORD,
the one we sinned against?
They refused to walk in his ways
and would not heed his instruction.
25So he poured out on them the heat of his anger and the violence of battle.
It set them ablaze on every side, yet they did not understand;
it burned them, yet they gave it no thought.
fields.summary: God’s servant will bring justice to the nations gently, not snapping off a split reed. All the earth is to sing a new song, but Israel, God’s servant, is blind and deaf.

fields.title: Isaiah 43
fields.body_html:
You belong to me

1But now the LORD, your Creator, Jacob,
the one who shaped you, Israel, says this:
Do not be afraid, for I have redeemed you.
I called you by your own name; you belong to me.
2When you go through the waters, I will be beside you;
through the rivers, they will not flood over you.
When you walk in the fire, you will not be scorched;
the flame will not burn you up.
3For I am the LORD your God;
I am the Holy One of Israel, your Savior.
I have given Egypt as the price of your freedom,
Cush and Seba in exchange for you.
4You are dear in my sight; you are held in honor, and I love you.
So I will hand over human lives for you,
whole peoples for your life.
5Do not be afraid, for I am at your side.
From the east I will lead your descendants back;
from the west I will gather you in.
6I will tell the north, “Release them!”
and the south, “Do not keep them back!
Bring my sons from far away,
and my daughters from the farthest edge of the earth,
7all who are called by my name,
each one I created for my glory,
each one I formed, yes, each one I made.”
8Bring out the blind people who have eyes,
the deaf who have ears.
9All the nations are gathered together; the peoples have assembled.
Which of them could announce this,
or make us hear the former things?
Let them produce their witnesses and be shown to be in the right;
let people hear them and say, “It is the truth.”
10You are my witnesses, declares the LORD,
and my servant, the one I have chosen,
so that you will come to know me, put your trust in me, and grasp that I am he.
Before me no god was ever shaped,
and none will come after me.

11It is I, I who am the LORD;
there is no savior but me.
12It was I who told it beforehand, I who saved, I who made it heard;
no foreign god was among you.
You are my witnesses, declares the LORD, and I am God.
13From the first day on, I am he;
there is no one who can rescue from my power.
I work, and who can undo it?

Something new in the wilderness

14The LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, says this:
For your sake I have sent an enemy against Babylon. I will bring all of them down in flight,
the Chaldeans, in the ships that once rang with their shouts.
15I am the LORD, your Holy One,
who created Israel, your King.

16The LORD says this,
the one who makes a road through the sea,
a path through surging waters,
17who brought out chariot and horse, army and warrior together:
they lay down and did not get up;
they went out, quenched like a wick:
18Do not call to mind the former things,
or brood over the things of long ago.
19See, I am about to do something new; even now it is sprouting.
Do you not recognize it?
I will cut a road through the wilderness
and make rivers flow in the barren land.
20Even the wild beasts will honor me, the jackals and the ostriches,
because I have put water in the wilderness, rivers in the barren land,
to give drink to my people, my chosen ones,
21the people I formed to be my own;
they will recount my praises.

Wearied by Israel’s sins

22Yet it was not on me that you called, Jacob;
you have grown tired of me, Israel.
