23No sheep for burnt offerings have you brought me;
with your sacrifices you have given me no honor.
I laid no burden of grain offerings on you;
I did not make you weary for the sake of frankincense.
24You have not spent silver to buy me fragrant cane
or filled me with the fat of your sacrifices.
Instead you have made me toil like a servant under your sins
and worn me out with your guilt.

25I, yes I, am the one who wipes out your rebellious acts for my own sake;
your sins I will not keep in mind.
26Remind me;
let us take this to court together.
Lay out your account, so that you may be declared in the right.
27Your earliest ancestor sinned,
and those who spoke for you rebelled against me.
28So I treated the leaders of the sanctuary as unholy;
I handed Jacob over to be destroyed
and Israel to be mocked.
fields.summary: God has redeemed Israel and called them by name; they belong to God. God is doing something new, making a way in the wilderness, though Israel has wearied God with their sins.

fields.title: Isaiah 44
fields.body_html:
Water and Spirit for the chosen people

1But now listen, Jacob, my servant,
Israel, the one I have chosen.
2The LORD says this, he who made you, who shaped you in the womb and will come to your aid:
Have no fear, Jacob, my servant,
Jeshurun, my chosen one.
3For I will pour out water on parched ground
and send streams across the dry land;
I will pour out my Spirit on your children,
and my blessing on those who come after you.
4They will shoot up among the grass
like poplars beside running streams.
5One will say, “I am the LORD’s”;
another will claim the name of Jacob;
another will write on the hand, “Belonging to the LORD,”
and take Israel as a name of honor.

The first and the last, and the gods made of wood

6The LORD, the King of Israel, its Redeemer, the LORD of Armies, says this:
I am the first and I am the last;
there is no god but me.
7Who can compare with me? Let him speak up, announce it, and set it out in order for me,
from the day I founded the people of long ago.
Let them make known what is coming, the things that are still to happen.
8Do not shake with dread or be afraid.
Did I not announce it to you long ago and make it known? You are my witnesses.
Is there any god apart from me?
There is no other Rock; I know of none.
9All who shape idols are nothing,
and the things they love do them no good.
Their own witnesses see nothing and know nothing, so that they will be put to shame.
10Who would shape a god or cast an idol
that brings no gain?
11Look, all who join with it will be put to shame;
its makers are only human.
Let them all assemble and stand up;
they will be filled with dread and put to shame together.
12The ironsmith takes his tool and works it over hot charcoal.
He beats it into shape with hammers,
working it with all the strength of his arm.
Yet he gets hungry and his strength runs out;
he has no water to drink and is worn out.
13The woodworker stretches out a measuring line
and sketches the shape with a stylus.
He carves it with planes and marks it out with a compass.
He makes it in the shape of a man,
as handsome as any human, to sit in a house.
14He sets out to cut down cedars.
He picks a holm oak or an oak
and leaves it to grow strong among the forest trees.
He plants a pine, and the rain makes it grow tall.
15It is wood for people to burn.
He takes some of it and gets warm;
he lights a fire and bakes his bread.
Then he makes a god as well, and bows down to it;
he carves an idol and falls on his face before it.
16He burns half of it in the fire.
Over that half he cooks meat and eats;
he roasts his meat and is full.
He warms himself as well, and says, “Aha!
I am warm; I can see the flames!”
17What is left he makes into a god, an idol of his own.
He falls down before it and worships;
he prays to it and says, “Rescue me, because you are my god!”
18They do not know, they do not understand;
their eyes are smeared shut so they cannot see,
and their hearts so they cannot grasp the truth.
19He does not think it over. He lacks the knowledge and the sense to say,
“I burned half of it in the fire; I baked bread on its coals too;
I roasted meat and ate.
And am I to turn what is left into an abomination?
Am I to bow down before a lump of wood?”
20He grazes on ashes.
A mind that has been fooled has led him off course.
He cannot rescue himself or ask,
“Is this thing in my right hand not a fraud?”

21Keep these things in mind, Jacob,
and you, Israel, for you are my servant.
I shaped you; you are my own servant, Israel.
You will never slip from my mind.
22Like a cloud I have wiped away your rebellious acts,
and your sins like a mist.
Come back to me; I have redeemed you.
23Ring out with joy, you heavens, because the LORD has acted!
Raise a shout, you depths below the earth!
Burst into joyful song, mountains, you forest too, and every tree within it!
For the LORD has redeemed Jacob,
and he will show his glory in Israel.

The Maker of all things names Cyrus

24The LORD, your Redeemer, who shaped you in the womb, says this:
I am the LORD, who made everything,
who alone stretched out the heavens,
who hammered out the earth with no one beside me,
25who brings to nothing the omens of the babblers
and makes the diviners look like fools,
who sends the wise into retreat and makes their knowledge foolishness,
26who makes good the word of his servant
and carries out the plan announced by his messengers,
who says of Jerusalem, “People will live in her again,” and of the towns of Judah, “They will be built again;
I will restore her ruins,”
27who says to the ocean depths, “Dry up!
I will make your rivers run dry,”
28who says of Cyrus, “He is my shepherd;
he will carry out everything I desire,”
and the word goes out about Jerusalem, “She will be built again,”
and to the temple, “Your foundations will be laid.”
fields.summary: God will pour out water and Spirit on the chosen people. God is the first and the last, idols made of wood are foolish, and the Maker of all things names Cyrus as the one who will rebuild Jerusalem.

fields.title: Isaiah 45
fields.body_html:
The LORD calls Cyrus by name

1The LORD says this to his anointed, to Cyrus,
whom I hold by the right hand to beat down nations before him
and undo the sword belts of kings,
to throw doors open ahead of him so that no gates stay shut:
2I myself will march ahead of you and flatten the rough ground.
I will smash bronze doors and hack through iron bars.
3I will hand over to you treasures kept in the dark
and wealth hoarded in hidden vaults.
Then you will know that I am the LORD; the God of Israel is calling you by name.
4It was for Jacob my servant, for Israel my chosen one,
that I called you by your name and honored you with a title,
even though you did not know me.
5I am the LORD; there is no one else.
Other than me, there is no God.
I will buckle your belt on you for battle, though you have not known me,
6so that people from where the sun rises to where it sets may know that there is none but me.
I am the LORD; there is no one else.
7I shape the light and I create the darkness;
I bring about peace and I create calamity.
I am the LORD, the one who does all of this.

8Heavens above, let righteousness trickle down;
clouds, let it stream out.
Earth, open up and yield a harvest of salvation, and let righteousness sprout along with it.
I, the LORD, have brought it into being.

The clay and the potter

9Woe to anyone who argues with the one who shaped him,
one shard among the shards of earthenware!
Does the clay ask its potter, “What do you think you are making?”
Does your handiwork say of you, “He has no hands”?

10Woe to anyone who says to a father, “What kind of child is this you are fathering?”
or to a woman in labor, “What is this you are giving birth to?”

11The LORD, the Holy One of Israel, the one who formed him, says this:
Ask me about what is coming!
Are you going to give me orders about my children, about the things my hands have made?
12I am the one who made the earth and created the human race to live on it.
With my own hands I spread out the heavens,
and I give orders to every star in them.
13I myself have roused him for my righteous purpose, and I will clear every path before him.
He will build my city again and release my exiled people, without ransom or bribe,
says the LORD of Armies.

14The LORD says this:
The harvests of Egypt, the trade goods of Cush, and the Sabeans, a towering people,
will pass into your hands and belong to you.
They will march behind you in chains;
they will cross over to you, bow low before you, and make their appeal to you:
“God really is in your midst! There is no one else; there is no other god at all.”
15You are indeed a God who hides himself,
God of Israel, who saves!
16Shame and humiliation will cover them all;
those who carve idols will walk away together, disgraced.
17Israel is saved by the LORD, a salvation that lasts for all time.
You will never be shamed or humiliated, through all the ages to come.

Salvation for the ends of the earth

18For the LORD says this, the creator of the heavens, the one who is God, who shaped the earth and made it, who set it firmly in place,
who did not create it to be a barren waste but formed it for people to live on:
I am the LORD; there is no one else.
19My words were not whispered in hiding, from some corner of a dark land.
I never told Jacob’s offspring, “Look for me, but you will find nothing.”
I am the LORD: what I say is righteous,
and what I announce is upright.
20Come, gather, approach together, you who escaped the nations!
People who haul their wooden idols around understand nothing,
praying to a god that has no power to save.
21Make your declaration and bring your evidence; let them plan their answer together!
Who made this known in times long past and announced it back then?
Was it not I, the LORD? No god exists other than me.
I am a God who is righteous and who saves,
and there is no one except me.
22Turn toward me and be saved, every corner of the earth!
I am God, and no one else is.
23I have taken an oath by myself;
a righteous word has gone out from my mouth and will not come back unfulfilled:
to me every knee will bow,
and every tongue will swear loyalty to me.
24Of me they will say, “Only in the LORD is there righteousness and strength.”
Everyone who burned with anger against him will come before him in shame.
25In the LORD all Israel’s descendants will be shown to be in the right,
and they will rejoice proudly in him.
fields.summary: God calls Cyrus by name to subdue nations for the sake of Israel. The clay does not question the potter, and the ends of the earth are called to turn to God and be saved.

fields.title: Isaiah 46
fields.body_html:
The gods of Babylon must be carried

1Bel crouches low; Nebo sinks down.
Their idols are left to pack animals and cattle.
The images you used to carry are packed up as cargo,
a load for exhausted animals.
2Together they crouch and stoop.
They cannot save the load,
and they themselves are led away as captives.

The God who carries Israel

3Listen to me, house of Jacob,
all who remain of the house of Israel,
you whom I have carried as my load since birth,
whom I have borne since you came from the womb.
4Until you are old I am he,
and until your hair turns gray I am the one who will carry you.
I made you, and I will lift you;
I will carry you and bring you to safety.

5Whom will you hold up as my likeness, or rank as my equal?
Whom will you set beside me, as though we were alike?
6Some empty gold from their purses and weigh out silver on the balance.
They pay a craftsman to shape it into a god,
then fall on their faces before it and bow low.
7They heave it onto their shoulders and haul it, and set it down where it belongs.
There it stays; it cannot budge from the spot.
A person may cry out to it, but it makes no reply;
it saves no one from distress.

God’s plan will stand

8Remember this and steady yourselves;
think it through again, you rebels.
9Remember what happened long ago, in ages past:
I alone am God, and there is no other;
I am God, and none can compare with me.
10From the start I announce how things will end,
and from ages past what has not yet happened.
I say that my plan will stand
and that I will carry out all that I desire.
11Out of the east I call a bird of prey,
from a far country the man who serves my plan.
I have spoken it, and I will bring it to pass;
I have shaped it, and I will see it done.

12Listen to me, you hard of heart,
standing far off from righteousness.
13My righteousness I have brought near; it is close at hand,
and my salvation will not linger.
In Zion I will set salvation,
and on Israel I will bestow my splendor.
fields.summary: The gods of Babylon must be carried as burdens, but God has carried Israel from birth, and God’s plan will stand.

fields.title: Isaiah 47
fields.body_html:
Daughter Babylon in the dust

1Get down and sit in the dirt, Virgin Daughter Babylon.
Sit on the bare ground, Daughter of the Chaldeans; your throne is gone.
Never again will anyone call you soft and pampered.
2Take the hand mill and grind the meal.
Off with your veil! Strip away your long skirt, bare your legs, and wade the rivers.
3Your nakedness will be laid bare; your disgrace will be there for all to see.
I will take vengeance, and I will hold back for no one.

4Our Redeemer, whose name is the LORD of Armies,
the Holy One of Israel!
5Sit there speechless; go off into the dark, Daughter of the Chaldeans,
for no one will hail you again as queen over the kingdoms.
6In my anger at my people, I let my own inheritance be defiled
and handed them over to your power.
Yet you showed them no compassion;
you loaded your heavy yoke even on the old.
7You told yourself, “I will be queen forever, for all time.”
You never took these things to heart or thought about where they would lead.

Spells and stargazers cannot save her

8So hear this now, you pleasure-loving woman, settled so securely,
who thinks in her heart, “I am, and there is no other but me.
I will never be left a widow; I will never know the grief of losing children.”
9Yet both will strike you in an instant, on a single day:
the loss of your children and widowhood.
They will fall on you in full force,
for all your many sorceries and all the strength of your spells.
10You leaned on your wickedness and said, “No one is watching me.”
Your wisdom and your learning have drawn you off course,
and in your heart you said, “I am, and there is no other but me.”
11Evil will come upon you, and you will not know the charm to drive it off;
ruin will fall on you that you cannot pay off;
destruction will overtake you all at once, something you never saw coming.
12Go on, then: hold your ground with your spells and your heaps of sorceries,
which you have worked at from your earliest days.
Maybe they will help you; maybe you will make your foes tremble.
13All the advice you gather only wears you out.
Let them come forward now and save you from what is coming upon you,
those who divide up the heavens and watch the stars,
who give their forecasts at each new moon.
14Look! They have become like straw, and fire consumes them.
They cannot rescue their own lives from the blaze.
This is not a bed of coals to warm yourself by, not a hearth to sit beside.
15That is all they will be to you, the people you have toiled with,
who have traded with you since your youth:
they stray off, each going a different way, and no one is left to save you.
fields.summary: Daughter Babylon is brought down into the dust, and her spells and stargazers cannot save her.

fields.title: Isaiah 48
fields.body_html:
Things foretold to a stubborn people

1Hear this, house of Jacob, you who bear the name Israel
and sprang from the waters of Judah,
you who swear by the name of the LORD and call on the God of Israel,
yet without truth and without righteousness.
2For they name themselves after the holy city
and lean for support on the God of Israel;
the LORD of Armies is his name.

3What came first I foretold long before;
it issued from my mouth, and I let it be heard.
Then all at once I acted, and it took place.
4Because I knew how unyielding you are,
your neck a cord of iron and your forehead bronze,
5so I announced them to you in advance;
I let you hear of them before they came,
so that you could never say, “My idol made them happen;
my carved image and my molten god decreed them.”
6You heard it; now see the whole of it.
Will you yourselves not testify to it?
From now on I make new things known to you,
things kept hidden that you never knew.
7Only now are they brought into being, not in days gone by;
until today you never heard of them.
So you cannot claim, “See, I knew that all along.”
8You have not heard and have not known;
long ago your ear stayed shut.
For I knew that you would surely prove faithless,
and you were named “Rebel from the womb.”
9To honor my name I am slow to let my anger loose;
for the sake of my praise I rein it in for your good,
so that I will not cut you off.
10See, I have put you through the refiner’s fire, but not as silver;
I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.
11For my own sake, for my own sake I act, for why should my name be dishonored?
I will not give my glory to another.

The first and the last

12Hear me, Jacob, Israel, the one I called:
I am he. I am the first; I am the last as well.
13My own hand set the earth on its foundations,
and my right hand stretched the heavens wide;
at my call they rise and stand together.
14All of you, gather and hear!
Which of them announced these things?
The one the LORD loves will carry out his purpose against Babylon,
and his arm will be turned against the Chaldeans.
15It is I, I myself, who have spoken; I also summoned him.
I have brought him, and he will carry his journey through to success.
16Come close to me and listen: never, from the start, have I spoken in hiding;
from the moment it began, I was present.
And now the Lord GOD has sent me, and his Spirit.

If only you had listened

17The LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, says this:
I am the LORD your God, who teaches you what is for your good
and guides you along the road you are to walk.
18If only you had heeded my commands!
Then your peace would have run like a river,
and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
19Your descendants would have been as many as the sand,
your own children like its grains;
their name would never be cut off or wiped out from my presence.
20Go out of Babylon! Escape from the Chaldeans!
Raise a joyful cry and tell it; let this be heard,
sent out to the far ends of the earth.
Say, “The LORD has redeemed his servant Jacob!”
21They knew no thirst as he guided them through dry wastes;
for them he brought water streaming out of the rock;
he broke the rock open, and out poured the water.
22There is no peace,
says the LORD, for the wicked.
fields.summary: God foretold these things to a stubborn people so they could not credit their idols. God is the first and the last, and if only they had listened, their peace would have been like a river.

fields.title: Isaiah 49
fields.body_html:
The servant called before birth

1Coastlands, listen to me;
peoples who live far away, give heed.
The LORD called me while I was still in the womb;
he spoke my name while I was yet inside my mother.
2He gave me a mouth as sharp as a sword
and kept me covered in the shade of his hand.
He shaped me into a keen, polished arrow
and tucked me away in his quiver.
3He said to me, “You are my servant, Israel;
in you I will make my beauty known.”
4But I said, “I have toiled for no purpose;
I have worn out my strength for what is empty, a mere breath.
Even so, my case rests with the LORD,
and my God holds my wages.”
5And now the LORD speaks, who shaped me in the womb to be his servant,
to turn Jacob back to him
and to gather Israel to him
(for I am honored in the eyes of the LORD,
and my God has become my strength),
6he says: “It is not enough that you should be my servant
to raise up the tribes of Jacob
and bring home the survivors of Israel.
I will make you a light for the nations as well,
so that you may be my salvation to the farthest edge of the earth.”

A time of favor and a road home

7The LORD, the Redeemer of Israel and its Holy One, says this to the one whom everyone despises, whom the nation detests, the servant of rulers:
Kings will see you and rise to their feet;
princes will see you and bow low,
because of the LORD, who keeps faith,
the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you.
8The LORD says this: In a time of favor I answered you;
on the day of salvation I came to your aid.
I will watch over you and give you to be a covenant for the people,
to set the land on its feet again
and to hand out once more its ruined estates,
9telling the prisoners, “Go free,”
and those in the dark, “Come out into the open.”
They will graze along the roads,
and every bare hilltop will be their grazing land.
10They will not go hungry or thirsty,
and neither the searing heat nor the sun will beat them down,
for the one who has mercy on them will be their guide;
he will bring them to springs of water.
11Every one of my mountains I will turn into a pathway,
and my main roads will be built up high.
12Look, they are coming from far away;
look, some from the north and from the west,
and some from the land of Sinim.
13Heavens, ring out with joy! Earth, be glad!
Mountains, break out in cries of joy!
For the LORD has comforted his people
and will show tender love to his suffering ones.

Zion is not forgotten

14But Zion said, “The LORD has left me behind;
the Lord has forgotten all about me.”
15Could a woman forget the baby she is nursing,
or stop feeling tender love for the son she carried?
Women such as these may forget,
but I will not forget you.
16Look, I have carved you into my palms;
your walls are never out of my sight.
17Your children are hurrying home,
while those who wrecked you and stripped you bare are leaving you.
18Raise your eyes and look in every direction:
they are all gathering and coming to you.
As I live, declares the LORD, you will put every one of them on like jewelry
and wrap them about you like a bride on her wedding day.
19Your ruins and your abandoned places,
your devastated land,
will now be too crowded for the people who live in them,
and those who devoured you will be long gone.
20The children born while you were mourning your losses will still say in your hearing,
“There is not enough room here for me; move aside so I can have a place to live.”
21Then you will ask yourself, “Who fathered these children for me?
I had lost my children and could bear no more;
I was exiled and cast aside. Who raised these?
I was left all by myself;
where have these been?”

22The Lord GOD says this: See, I will raise my hand to beckon the nations
and lift my signal flag for the peoples.
They will carry your sons home in their arms,
and your daughters will ride on their shoulders.
23Kings will look after your children as guardians, and their princesses will nurse them for you.
They will bow low before you with their faces to the ground
and lick the dust off your feet.
Then you will know that I am the LORD,
and that none who wait in hope for me end up ashamed.

24Can loot be pulled from a warrior’s grasp?
Can captives held by one who is in the right get free?
25But the LORD says this: Yes, a warrior’s captives will be taken from him,
and a tyrant’s loot will slip out of his hands.
I myself will take on the one who fights you,
and I myself will rescue your children.
26Those who oppress you I will feed with their own flesh,
and they will get drunk on their own blood as if it were new wine.
Then all humankind will know that I, the LORD, am the one who saves you,
your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
fields.summary: The servant, called before birth, will be a light to the nations. In a time of favor God will bring the people home, and God will never forget Zion, as a mother cannot forget her child.

fields.title: Isaiah 50
fields.body_html:
Where is your mother’s divorce document?

1The LORD says this: Where is the certificate of divorce I gave your mother when I sent her away?
Or was it to one of my creditors that I handed you over in payment?
No, it was for your own guilt that you were sold,
and for your rebellions that your mother was sent away.
2When I came, why was no one there? When I called, why did no one reply?
Is my hand so short that it cannot ransom,
or do I lack the power to rescue?
With a single rebuke I drain the sea dry and turn rivers into wasteland.
Their fish rot where the water has gone, and they perish from thirst.
3I dress the skies in black
and wrap them in sackcloth like a cloak.

The servant who listens and does not turn back

4The Lord GOD has given me the tongue of one who is taught,
so that I know how to bear up the weary with a word.
Each morning he rouses me;
he rouses my ear to listen as a learner listens.
5The Lord GOD has opened my ear,
and I have not resisted;
I have not turned away and gone back.
6I let those who struck me have my back,
and those who tore at my beard have my cheeks.
I did not turn my face away from insult and spit.
7The Lord GOD is my help,
so disgrace has not overcome me.
That is why I have made my face like flint,
and I know I will not be put to shame.
8The one who will declare me in the right is close at hand.
Who will take me to court? Let us stand up side by side.
Who has a case against me? Let him step forward and face me.
9Yes, the Lord GOD stands by me;
who then can pronounce me guilty?
All of them will fall apart like worn-out clothes,
and the moth will devour them.
10Who among you fears the LORD and listens to the voice of his servant?
Let the one who walks in darkness, with no glimmer of light,
trust in the name of the LORD and lean on his God.
11But all of you who light a fire and arm yourselves with blazing torches,
go on, walk by the glare of your own fire, among the torches you have set alight!
From my hand you will receive this:
you will lie down in agony.
fields.summary: The people were sold for their sins, not divorced. The servant listens to God each morning and does not turn back from those who strike him.

fields.title: Isaiah 51
fields.body_html:
Look to the rock you were cut from

1Listen to me, you who chase after righteousness, you who seek the LORD:
look to the rock you were cut from,
to the hollow of the pit you were dug out of.
2Look to Abraham your ancestor
and to Sarah, who gave birth to your people.
When I called him he was a single man,
yet I blessed him and made him many.

3For the LORD will comfort Zion; he will bring comfort to all her ruined places.
He will make her wilderness like Eden,
her barren plain like the garden of the LORD.
Gladness and delight will be found in her,
songs of thanks and the sound of music.

4Listen closely to me, my people;
hear me, my nation.
Instruction will go out from me,
and I will make my justice stand firm as a light for the peoples.
5My righteousness is close; my salvation has set out,
and my arms will judge the peoples.
The coastlands look to me in hope,
and they wait for my arm.
6Raise your eyes to the sky and look at the earth below.
The sky will drift away like smoke, the earth will fray like old clothing,
and those who live on it will die like gnats.
But my salvation will remain forever,
and my righteousness will never give way.

7Hear me, you who know what is right,
you people who carry my instruction in your hearts:
do not be afraid when mortals mock you,
and do not lose heart at their abuse.
8Like clothing, they will be eaten by moths;
like wool, they will be chewed by grubs.
But my righteousness will stand forever,
my salvation through every generation.

Awake, arm of the LORD

9Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of the LORD!
Awake as in days long gone, in ages past!
Was it not you who cut Rahab to pieces,
who ran the sea monster through?
10Was it not you who drained the sea,
the waters of the vast deep,
and turned the sea’s depths into a road for the redeemed to cross?
11Those the LORD has ransomed will come back; they will enter Zion with glad shouts,
with joy that never ends resting on their heads.
Delight and gladness will catch up with them,
and grief and groaning will run away.

12I, I am he who comforts you.
Who are you, to be afraid of mortals who die,
of human beings who wither like grass,
13and you have forgotten the LORD your Maker, who spread out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth?
Day after day you live in constant dread of the oppressor’s rage
as he takes aim to destroy.
But where is the oppressor’s rage now?
14The one bent low in chains will soon be released;
he will not die and go down to the pit,
nor will he go without bread.
15I am the LORD your God,
who stirs up the sea until its waves roar;
the LORD of Armies is his name.
16I have put my words in your mouth
and sheltered you in the shadow of my hand,
to plant the heavens and lay the foundations of the earth,
and to say to Zion, “You are my people.”

The cup of wrath taken away

17Awake, awake! Stand up, Jerusalem,
you who have drunk from the LORD’s hand the cup of his wrath,
who have drunk the goblet that makes people reel and emptied it to the bottom.
18Of all the children she bore, there is not one to guide her;
of all the children she raised, there is no one to take her by the hand.
19These two disasters have come upon you;
who will grieve for you?
Devastation and ruin, famine and sword: how can I comfort you?
20Your children have collapsed; they lie at the corner of every street like an antelope in a net,
filled to the brim with the wrath of the LORD, the rebuke of your God.
21So hear this, you who are afflicted,
you who are drunk but not with wine:

22Your Lord, the LORD, your God who takes up his people’s cause, says this:
See, I have taken out of your hand the cup that makes you reel.
The goblet of my wrath you will never drink again.
23I will put it into the hands of those who tormented you,
who said to you, “Lie face down, so we can walk across you.”
And you made your back like the ground,
like a street for people to walk on.
fields.summary: The people are told to look to Abraham and Sarah, the rock they were cut from. The arm of God is called to awake, and the cup of wrath is taken from Jerusalem.

fields.title: Isaiah 52
fields.body_html:
Zion, rise from the dust

1Wake up, wake up, Zion; wrap yourself in your strength!
Jerusalem, holy city, dress in your robes of beauty,
for never again will anyone uncircumcised or unclean come into you.
2Shake the dust from yourself and stand, Jerusalem, held captive!
Undo the cords that bind your neck, captive Daughter Zion.

3For the LORD says this: You were sold and nothing was paid; you will be redeemed and no silver will change hands. 4For the Lord GOD says this: Long ago my people went down to Egypt to stay there as foreigners; then Assyria crushed them without cause. 5So now, what is here for me? declares the LORD. My people have been taken, and nothing was paid for them. Their rulers howl, declares the LORD, and all day long, without pause, my name is scorned. 6That is why my people will come to know my name. That is why, on that day, they will know that I am he, the one who speaks: Here I am!
7What a welcome sight on the mountains, the feet of one who brings good news! He calls out peace, he brings word of good things, he announces salvation,
and he tells Zion, “Your God reigns!”
8Hear it! Your watchmen are raising a shout; they cry out for joy as one,
for they see it plainly, eye to eye, as the LORD comes back to Zion.
9You ruined places of Jerusalem, break into song; shout for joy, all of you together!
The LORD has brought comfort to his people;
he has redeemed Jerusalem.
10The LORD has stripped bare his holy arm in full view of every nation,
and the whole earth, to its farthest edges, will see the salvation of our God.

Go out and be pure

11Depart, depart, get out of there!
Touch nothing unclean.
Leave from the midst of her and make yourselves pure,
you who bear the vessels of the LORD.
12For you will not leave in a rush,
nor go off like runaways.
The LORD walks at your head,
and the God of Israel guards you from behind.

The servant raised high

13Look, my servant will act with insight and succeed.
He will rise and be lifted up; he will stand very high.
14Just as many stared at you in horror
(his appearance so ruined it no longer seemed a man’s,
his form so marred it hardly looked human),
15so he will sprinkle many nations.
Kings will fall silent before him,
for they will see a thing no one ever told them
and grasp a thing they never heard.
fields.summary: Zion is called to rise from the dust, for God has redeemed Jerusalem, and the feet of the messenger bring good news. The servant will be raised high.

fields.title: Isaiah 53
fields.body_html:
The servant who bore the sin of many

1Who has believed the news that reached us?
And the arm of the LORD, to whom has it been laid bare?
2He grew up before him like a little shoot, like a root coming up from parched earth.
He had no stately form, no splendor to draw our eyes,
no fine looks to make us long for him.
3He was despised and shunned by everyone,
a man of pains, no stranger to sickness.
People turned their faces away from him;
he was despised, and we counted him as nothing.
4Yet it was our sicknesses that he bore,
our pains that he shouldered,
while we took him for a man under a plague,
beaten down by God and brought low.
5But it was for our rebellions that he was pierced through,
for our guilt that he was crushed.
On him fell the discipline that won our peace,
and his welts have brought us healing.
6Every one of us has wandered off like sheep;
we have each turned aside down our own path,
and the LORD has made all our guilt fall on him.
7He was hard pressed, and he bowed low under it, yet he did not open his mouth.
Like a young sheep led off to be slaughtered,
like a ewe silent in front of those who shear her,
he did not open his mouth.
8He was taken off by a cruel judgment,
and of the people of his day, who gave it a thought?
For he was torn from the land of the living;
because my people rebelled, the blow fell on him.
9His burial was set among the wicked,
and he lay with a rich man in death,
although he had never done violence or spoken deceit.
10Yet it pleased the LORD to crush him and make him sick.
If he offers himself as a guilt offering,
he will see children and live long days,
and through his hands what pleases the LORD will thrive.
11After all his soul’s hard labor he will see, and he will have his fill.
My servant, the righteous one, will make the many righteous by his knowledge,
and he will shoulder their guilt.
12So I will give him a share among the many, and he will split the spoils with the mighty,
because he emptied out his life to the point of death
and was reckoned among the rebels.
It was he who bore the sin of many,
and he pleads on behalf of the rebels.
fields.summary: The servant was despised and shunned, wounded for the people’s sins and crushed for their wrongdoing, led like a lamb to the slaughter. He bore the sin of many, and God will give him a portion among the great.

fields.title: Isaiah 54
fields.body_html:
The childless wife will have many children

1Sing out, childless woman who never bore a child;
burst into song and shout, you who never went into labor!
For the woman left alone will have more children than the woman who has a husband, says the LORD.
2Make room in your tent; let the curtains of your dwellings be spread wide, and hold nothing back.
Let out your tent ropes
and drive your pegs in firmly.
3For you will burst out to the right and to the left;
your descendants will take over the lands of nations
and fill ruined cities with people again.
4Have no fear; you will not be put to shame.
Do not hang your head; no disgrace will come to you.
You will forget the shame you bore when young
and no longer call to mind the scorn you suffered as a widow.
5Your husband is the one who made you;
the LORD of Armies is his name.
Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel,
and he is called God of the whole earth.
6For the LORD calls to you as to a wife left alone and grieving in spirit,
as to the wife a man married young and then cast off, says your God.
7I forsook you for a passing moment,
but with vast compassion I will gather you in.
8When my anger overflowed, I turned my face away from you for a moment;
but with loyal love that lasts forever I will show you compassion,
says the LORD, your Redeemer.

A promise as firm as the oath to Noah

9This is for me as it was with the waters of Noah.
Just as I took an oath that Noah’s flood would never again sweep over the earth,
so I take an oath now: I will not be angry with you or rebuke you.
10The mountains may move away
and the hills may totter,
yet my loyal love will never move away from you, and my covenant of peace will not totter,
says the LORD, who shows you compassion.

A city built of precious stones

11Poor wretched city, battered by storms and left without comfort,
look: I will set your stones in dark mortar
and lay your foundations with sapphires.
12I will crown your towers with rubies,
build your gates of fiery gems,
and make your whole outer wall of costly stones.
13The LORD will teach every one of your children,
and great peace will be theirs.
14You will be set firm in righteousness.
Stay far from oppression, for you will have nothing to fear,
and from terror, for it will not draw near you.
15Should anyone pick a fight with you, it does not come from me;
whoever attacks you will fall before you.
16Look: I made the metalworker who blows on the burning charcoal
and turns out a weapon for its use.
I also made the one who destroys, to bring ruin.
17Not one weapon shaped to harm you will succeed,
and every tongue that accuses you in court you will prove wrong.
This is the share that belongs to the servants of the LORD; their righteousness comes from me, declares the LORD.
fields.summary: The barren woman is told to sing, for she will have many children. God’s promise of peace is as firm as the oath to Noah, and Zion will be built of precious stones.

fields.title: Isaiah 55
fields.body_html:
Free food and drink for all who thirst

1Listen, all who thirst: come down to the water!
You who have no silver,
come, buy grain and eat.
Come, buy grain, wine and milk, and pay nothing for them.
2Why pay out silver for what is not bread,
and the fruit of your work for what never fills you?
Pay close attention to me: eat what is good,
and let your appetite delight in the finest food.
3Turn your ears this way and come to me;
hear me, and you will truly live.
I will grant you a covenant that stands forever:
the loyal love I pledged to David, which does not fail.
4Look: I set him up as a witness to the peoples,
a prince who gave orders to nations.
5You in turn will summon a nation you have never known,
and a nation that never knew you will hurry to you,
drawn by the LORD your God,
the Holy One of Israel, who has made you shine with honor.

A call to return, and a word that does its work

6Look for the LORD while he can still be found;
call to him while he is close by.
7Let those who do wrong leave their path behind,
and the evil their schemes.
Let them come back to the LORD, and he will show them mercy;
let them come back to our God, for he is generous to forgive.
8What I plan is not what you plan,
and the paths you take are not my paths,
declares the LORD.
9As far as the heavens tower over the earth,
so far do my ways tower over yours,
and my thoughts over yours.
10Just as rain and snow fall from the heavens and do not go back up
until they have soaked the ground
and made it bud and grow,
giving seed to the one who sows
and bread to the one who eats,
11so it is with the word that leaves my mouth:
it will not come back to me with nothing done,
but it will do what I want
and succeed in the errand I sent it on.
12You will set out with gladness
and be guided along in peace.
Mountains and hills will ring with shouts of joy ahead of you,
and every tree in the fields will clap its hands.
13Where thornbushes grew, cypress trees will rise;
where nettles grew, myrtle will spring up.
This will win the LORD a name,
a sign that will last forever and never be cut down.
fields.summary: All who are thirsty are invited to come and receive food and drink without cost. They are called to seek God while God may be found, for God’s word will do what God sends it to do.

fields.title: Isaiah 56
fields.body_html:
A house of prayer for all peoples

1The LORD says this:
Guard justice and practice righteousness,
for my salvation is near and ready to come,
and my righteousness is about to be made known.
2How blessed is the mortal who does this,
the human being who clings to it,
who guards the Sabbath and does not make it common,
and who will not lift a hand to do any evil.

3The foreigner who has attached himself to the LORD must not say,
“The LORD is sure to set me apart from his people.”
The eunuch must not say,
“See, I am nothing but a dried-up tree.”

4For the LORD says this to the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths,
who choose what gives me pleasure,
and who hold firmly to my covenant:
5within my house and inside my walls I will set up for them a monument and a name worth more than sons and daughters.
I will give each of them a name that lasts forever,
one that will never be wiped out.

6As for the foreigners who attach themselves to the LORD, who serve him,
who love the name of the LORD and become his servants,
everyone who guards the Sabbath and does not make it common
and who clings to my covenant,
7I will lead them to my holy mountain and make them glad in my house of prayer.
Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will find favor on my altar,
for my house will be named a house of prayer for all peoples.
8So declares the Lord GOD, who collects the scattered people of Israel:
I will yet bring more to join them, beyond the ones already brought together.
9Every creature that roams the fields,
every beast in the forest, come here and devour!

Blind watchmen and greedy shepherds

10The nation’s lookouts are blind, every one; none of them understands.
All of them are voiceless dogs that cannot give a bark;
they sprawl out and dream, and dozing is what they love.
11The dogs are ravenous; they never know when they have had enough.
And these are the shepherds! They have no discernment.
They have all gone off their own way,
every one of them grabbing what he can get.
12“Come on,” they call, “I will bring the wine; let us soak ourselves in beer!
Tomorrow will be like today,
a grand day, with plenty and to spare.”
fields.summary: Foreigners and eunuchs who keep the covenant will be welcomed, for God’s house will be a house of prayer for all peoples. Israel’s watchmen are blind and its shepherds greedy.

fields.title: Isaiah 57
fields.body_html:
The righteous perish and the idols fail

1The righteous person perishes,
and no one gives it a thought.
Those who show loyal love are gathered away, and no one sees
that the righteous is gathered away from the evil.
2He goes in to peace.
Those who walk the straight way find rest on their beds.
3As for you, step up here, you children of a witch,
you breed of an adulterer and a prostitute!
4Who is it you are jeering at?
At whom do you open your mouths wide and stick out your tongues?
Are you not children born of rebellion, offspring of lies,
5you who inflame yourselves with lust among the oaks,
under every leafy tree,
who butcher children in the stream beds
below the clefts of the cliffs?
6With the smooth stones of the stream bed lies your share;
those, those are your allotment.
Even to them you have poured out drink offerings and lifted up grain offerings.
Am I to be soothed by this?
7On a mountain high and lifted up you have laid out your bed,
and there too you have gone up to offer sacrifice.
8Behind the door and its doorpost
you have put your reminder.
You deserted me: you stripped, climbed in, and made your bed wide. You struck a bargain with them for yourself;
you loved their bed; you gazed at their nakedness.
9You went to the king with olive oil
and heaped up your perfumes.
You sent your envoys far away,
and you sank down as far as Sheol.
10You wore yourself out with all your traveling,
yet you never said, “It is no use.”
Your arm found fresh life,
so you did not give way.
11Whom did you dread so much, whom did you fear, that you turned false,
and did not remember me or give me a thought?
Was it that I stayed silent so long
that you no longer fear me?
12I will lay bare what you call your righteousness,
and your deeds as well; they will be of no use to you.
13When you call for help, let your crowd of idols rescue you!
The wind will sweep every one of them away; a puff of air will carry them off.
But whoever takes shelter in me will receive the land as an inheritance
and will own my holy mountain.
14Then the word will go out: “Raise a highway, raise it up, clear a path!
Lift every stumbling block out of the road my people travel.”

The high God with the crushed and lowly

15For the One high and lifted up, who dwells in eternity, whose name is Holy, says this:
My home is the high and holy place,
yet I am also with the one who is crushed and low in spirit,
to bring the spirit of the lowly back to life
and put new life into the hearts of the crushed.
16For I will not press my case forever,
nor stay angry for all time;
otherwise the human spirit would grow faint before me,
the breath of life that I myself made.
17Because of his sinful greed I was angry; I struck him, hid my face, and was angry still.
Yet he kept turning away, going the way his own heart chose.
18I have seen the paths he has taken, but I will heal him.
I will guide him
and give back comfort to him, and to those among his people who mourn.
19I bring into being the fruit of the lips:
Peace, peace, to those far off and to those close at hand, says the LORD, and I will heal them.
20But the wicked are like the churning sea
that can never lie calm;
its waters cast up muck and mud.
21There is no peace,
says my God, for the wicked.
fields.summary: The righteous perish and idols fail those who trust them, but God, who dwells on high, also lives with the crushed and the lowly.

fields.title: Isaiah 58
fields.body_html:
The fast that God chooses

1Shout with all your strength; hold nothing back.
Let your voice ring out like a ram’s horn.
Make known to my people how they have rebelled,
and to the house of Jacob what their sins are.
2Day after day they come looking for me
and seem glad to learn my ways,
acting like a nation that does righteousness and has not turned away from the justice of its God.
They ask me for rulings that are right;
drawing near to God gives them pleasure.
3“We have fasted,” they say, “so why do you not see?
We have humbled ourselves, so why do you not notice?”
But look: on the very day you fast, you pursue your own business
and drive all your laborers hard.
4Look, you fast, and then you wrangle and brawl
and hit out with a vicious fist.
Fasting the way you do now
will never carry your voice up to the heights.
5Do you think this is the fast I choose:
a day when people deny themselves,
droop their heads like a bulrush, and make their bed on sackcloth and ashes?
Do you call that a fast,
a day that wins the favor of the LORD?
6No, this is the fast I choose:
loose the bonds that wickedness has tied,
untie the ropes of the yoke,
send the crushed away free,
and tear every yoke in two.
7Is it not to break your bread with someone who is hungry,
to take the wandering poor into your home,
to clothe the naked person you meet,
and never to turn your back on your own kin?
8Then like the dawn your light will break forth,
and your healing will spring up without delay.
Your righteousness will march ahead of you,
and the glory of the LORD will guard you from behind.
9Then when you call, the LORD will answer;
when you cry out for help, he will say, “I am here.”
If you do away with the yoke among you,
the finger pointed in scorn, and words that do harm,
10if you give of yourself to the hungry
and meet the needs of those who suffer,
then your light will dawn in the darkness,
and your gloom will be like the brightness of midday.
11The LORD will guide you without ceasing.
He will satisfy your hunger in a sunbaked land
and give strength to your bones.
You will be like a garden with plenty of water,
like a spring whose flow never stops.
12Your people will build again the ruins left from long ago;
you will raise up foundations laid generations back.
You will be named the one who closes the gap in the wall,
the one who makes the roads fit to live beside.
13If you hold back your steps on the Sabbath
and do not chase your own interests on my holy day;
if you name the Sabbath a delight, the holy day of the LORD a day to honor,
and honor it by leaving your own paths, your own pursuits, and your deal-making aside,
14then you will find joy in the LORD.
I will set you astride the high places of the land
and nourish you from the inheritance of Jacob your father.
For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
fields.summary: God rejects fasting that is only for show; the fast God chooses is to loose the bonds of injustice, share bread with the hungry and shelter the poor.

fields.title: Isaiah 59
fields.body_html:
Sin confessed and a Redeemer for Zion

1See, the hand of the LORD is not too short to save,
nor has his ear become too heavy to hear.
2Rather, your guilt has set up a barrier between you and your God,
and your sins have made him turn his face away from you, so that he does not listen.
3Blood has defiled your palms,
and guilt your fingers.
Your lips have told lies;
your tongue keeps muttering what is unjust.
4No one brings a suit in righteousness;
no one argues a case honestly.
They lean on empty words and tell lies;
they are pregnant with mischief and bring wickedness into the world.
5They hatch adders’ eggs
and weave spiders’ webs.
Eat one of their eggs and you die;
crack one open and out comes a viper.
6Their webs will never make a garment,
and nothing they produce will cover them.
All they produce is wicked work;
their hands are full of violent deeds.
7Their feet race toward evil;
they are quick to spill innocent blood.
Their minds are full of wicked schemes;
ruin and wreckage lie along their roads.
8They do not know the road of peace,
and their tracks show no justice.
They have twisted their paths;
no one who walks on them knows peace.
9So justice stays far away from us,
and righteousness never catches up with us.
We wait in hope for light, and see only darkness;
we wait for the glow of dawn, yet we go on walking in the gloom.
10We fumble along the wall as blind people do,
groping as if we had no eyes.
At high noon we trip as though night were falling;
among those full of strength we are no better than corpses.
11We growl like bears, every one of us,
and coo our grief like doves.
We wait for justice, and none comes;
for salvation, and it keeps its distance from us.
12For our rebellious acts pile up before you,
and our sins speak as witnesses against us.
Our rebellion stays with us,
and we know our guilt well.
13We have rebelled and been false to the LORD;
we have turned away from following our God.
We have spoken of oppression and revolt,
and from our hearts we have conceived and voiced lying words.
14Justice is pushed back,
and righteousness keeps its distance.
Truth trips and falls in the city square,
and honesty can find no way in.
15Truth has gone missing,
and the one who keeps away from evil is robbed for it.
The LORD saw this, and it was evil in his sight that justice was gone.
16He saw that no one was there,
and he was dismayed that no one stepped in.
So his own arm won him the victory,
and his righteousness held him up.
17He put on righteousness as a coat of armor
and set the helmet of salvation on his head.
He dressed in vengeance for clothing,
and drew zeal around him like a robe.
18As they have acted, so he will repay them:
fury for his foes,
payment in full for his enemies;
even the coastlands he will repay in kind.
19In the west they will fear the name of the LORD,
and in the east, where the sun rises, they will fear his glory.
For he will come like a river forced through a narrow gorge,
a torrent driven by the wind of the LORD.
20To Zion a Redeemer will come,
to the people of Jacob who turn away from their rebellion,
declares the LORD.
21As for me, this is the covenant I make with them, says the LORD: my Spirit who rests on you and my words that I have set in your mouth will never leave your lips, nor the lips of your children, nor the lips of their children after them, says the LORD, from this day on and for all time.
fields.summary: The people’s sins have separated them from God, and they confess them. God puts on righteousness like armor and comes as a Redeemer to Zion.

fields.title: Isaiah 60
fields.body_html:
Zion’s light has come

1Rise up and shine, for your light has come;
the glory of the LORD has dawned over you.
2Look: darkness will cover the earth
and a heavy gloom will lie on the peoples,
but the LORD will rise like the dawn over you,
and his glory will be seen above you.
3Nations will make their way to your light,
and kings to the bright glow of your sunrise.
4Look up and gaze around you:
they are all gathering and coming to you.
Your sons will arrive from far away,
and your daughters will be carried on the hip like little children.
5Then you will look, and your face will glow;
your heart will tremble and open wide,
because the riches of the sea will be poured out on you
and the wealth of the nations will come to you.
6Caravans of camels will fill your land, young camels from Midian and Ephah.
Everyone from Sheba will come,
bringing gold and frankincense
and announcing the deeds of the LORD that deserve praise.
7Every flock of Kedar will be herded to you,
and the rams of Nebaioth will be at your service.
They will be offered on my altar and I will accept them,
and I will adorn the house that is my splendor.
8Who are these, speeding along like a cloud,
like doves returning to their roosting holes?
9The coastlands wait in hope for me; the ships of Tarshish sail first,
carrying your children home from distant places,
and their silver and gold along with them,
for the name of the LORD your God,
for the Holy One of Israel, since he has made you glorious.
10People from foreign lands will rebuild your walls,
and their kings will wait on you.
In my anger I struck you down,
but in my goodwill I have shown you tender mercy.
11Your gates will never be closed; day and night they will be left open,
so that the riches of the nations may be carried in to you,
with their kings brought along in the procession.
12Any nation or kingdom that refuses to serve you will be destroyed;
such nations will be left in complete ruin.
13The glory of Lebanon will be brought to you,
the juniper, the elm and the box tree side by side,
to adorn the site of my sanctuary,
and I will bring honor to the place where my feet rest.
14The children of those who oppressed you will come to you with heads bowed;
everyone who looked down on you will fall at your feet.
They will name you City of the LORD,
Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
15You were abandoned and despised, a place no traveler would cross;
but I will make you a source of pride for all time,
a delight to one generation after another.
16Nations will feed you with their milk,
and kings will nurse you like a child at the breast.
Then you will know that I, the LORD, am the one who saves you,
your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
17In place of bronze I will bring you gold; in place of iron, silver;
bronze where there was wood, and iron where there were stones.
I will make peace your governor
and righteousness your ruler.
18The sound of violence will never again be heard in your land,
nor of ruin and wreckage inside your borders.
You will give your walls the name Salvation
and your gates the name Praise.
19No longer will the sun be what lights your day,
nor the glow of the moon what shines on you;
the LORD will be your light for all time,
and your God will be your splendor.
20Your sun will set no more,
and your moon will never fade;
the LORD will be your light for all time,
and your days of grief will be over.
21Every one of your people will be righteous,
and the land will be theirs for all time.
They are a young branch my own hand has set in the ground, the work of my hands, to show my beauty.
22The smallest family among you will grow to a thousand,
the weakest into a strong nation.
I am the LORD; when the time is right, I will bring it about quickly.
fields.summary: Zion’s light has come and the glory of God has risen on her; nations will come to her light, and God will be her everlasting light.

fields.title: Isaiah 61
fields.body_html:
Good news for the lowly

1The Spirit of the Lord GOD rests on me,
for the LORD has anointed me to carry good news to the lowly.
He has sent me to bandage hearts that are broken,
to announce freedom for captives and, for those in chains, eyes opened wide,
2to announce a year when the LORD shows favor
and a day when our God takes vengeance,
to console all who grieve,
3to provide for those who mourn in Zion, to give them a festive turban in place of ashes,
the oil of rejoicing in place of grief,
a cloak of praise in place of a spirit burning low.
They will be named oaks of righteousness,
planted by the LORD to show his beauty.
4They will build up what has lain in ruins since long ago
and restore places left empty in their ancestors’ time;
they will make new again the wrecked cities,
deserted for one generation after another.
5Outsiders will stand ready to pasture your flocks,
and people from foreign lands will plow your fields and tend your vines.
6And you will be known as priests of the LORD;
people will speak of you as those who serve our God.
You will live on the wealth of the nations
and take pride in their glory.
7In place of your shame you will have a double share;
instead of disgrace they will sing out over what is given them.
So in their own land they will take possession of a double share,
and joy that never ends will belong to them.
8For I, the LORD, am a lover of justice
and I hate robbery joined to wrongdoing.
I will pay them their wages faithfully
and make a covenant with them that lasts forever.
9Their children will be famous among the nations,
and their descendants among the peoples.
Anyone who sees them will recognize them
as a line of children whom the LORD has blessed.

Dressed in salvation

10My joy in the LORD overflows; my whole being delights in my God.
He has dressed me in clothing of salvation
and wrapped me in a cloak of righteousness,
like a bridegroom wearing a turban as a priest does,
like a bride decked out in her jewels.
11As the ground pushes up its new growth,
as a garden makes its seeds break through the soil,
so the Lord GOD will make righteousness and praise grow up in full view of every nation.
fields.summary: The Spirit of God anoints the messenger to bring good news to the poor and to proclaim the year of God’s favor. Zion is dressed in garments of salvation.

fields.title: Isaiah 62
fields.body_html:
A new name for Zion

1Because of Zion I will not be silent,
and because of Jerusalem I will not keep still,
until her righteousness breaks out like daybreak
and her salvation burns like a torch.
2Nations will see your righteousness
and every king your glory.
You will be given a new name,
one that the LORD will pronounce with his own mouth.
3You will be a beautiful crown held in the hand of the LORD,
a king’s turban resting in the palm of your God.
4No one will call you Abandoned any longer,
or call your land Desolation.
Instead you will be named She Is My Delight, and your land Wedded,
because the LORD delights in you,
and your land will be taken as a bride.
5Your sons will take you
as a young man takes a young woman in marriage;
your God will be glad over you
with a groom’s joy over his bride.
6I have stationed guards on your walls, Jerusalem;
through the whole day and the whole night they will keep calling out, never silent.
You who keep reminding the LORD,
do not rest,
7and do not let him rest either,
until he has made Jerusalem secure and made her a city the whole earth praises.
8The LORD has bound himself by oath, by his right hand and his strong arm:
I will not let your enemies eat your grain any more,
nor let outsiders drink the new wine you worked to make,
9no, the ones who reaped the grain will eat it, praising the LORD,
and the ones who picked the grapes will drink the wine in the courtyards of my holy house.

Open a road for the people

10Through the gates, go through!
Open a road for the people!
Pile it up, pile up the highway, and pick out the stones!
Lift a signal flag high over the peoples!
11See, the LORD has announced to the farthest parts of the earth:
Tell Daughter Zion,
“Look, your salvation is coming!
Look, he brings his prize with him;
what he has won goes ahead of him.”
12They will be named The Holy People, Those the LORD Has Redeemed,
and you will be named Sought After, The City Not Abandoned.
fields.summary: Zion will receive a new name, and God will rejoice over her as a bridegroom over a bride. The people are to open a road for those coming home.

fields.title: Isaiah 63
fields.body_html:
The one coming from Edom

1Who is this arriving from Edom, coming from Bozrah with clothing dyed red,
so majestic in his robes,
pressing on in his immense strength?
It is I, who speak in righteousness, with great power to save.
2Why are your robes so red?
Why do your clothes look like those of a man stamping grapes in a winepress?
3Alone I have trampled the grapes in the press; from the peoples no one joined me.
In my anger I stamped on them;
in my fury I crushed them underfoot.
Their juice splashed across my garments,
and every piece of my clothing is stained.
4For I had set my heart on a day of vengeance,
and the year for redeeming my own had come.
5I looked around, and there was no one to help;
I stared, dismayed, and no one came to support.
So my own arm brought me victory,
and my fury kept me going.
6I crushed peoples underfoot in my anger;
I made them drunk on my fury,
and I let their lifeblood run down to the earth.

Remembering the loyal love of the LORD

7I will bring to mind the acts of loyal love the LORD has shown,
the deeds that make the LORD worthy of praise,
for all that the LORD has done for us:
the great goodness he has shown to the house of Israel,
out of his tender mercy and his abundant loyal love.
8He said, “Without doubt they are my people,
children who will not be false to me.”
So he became the one who saved them.
9Whenever they were in trouble, it troubled him, and the angel of his presence rescued them.
In his love and his pity he redeemed them;
he picked them up and carried them throughout the ages long past.
10But they rebelled and caused his Holy Spirit grief,
so he changed into their enemy and went to war against them himself.
11Then his people thought back to ancient times, to the days of Moses:
“Where is the one who brought them, with the shepherds of his flock, up out of the sea?
Where is the one who put his Holy Spirit in their midst,
12who made his glorious arm march at Moses’ right side,
who split the waters in front of them
to win himself a name that lasts forever,
13who guided them through the depths,
so that they did not stumble, sure-footed as a horse on the open plain?”
14As cattle make their way down into a valley,
the Spirit of the LORD brought them to rest.
In this way you guided your people, to make for yourself a name full of splendor.
15Look down from the heavens;
see from your exalted dwelling, holy and splendid!
What has become of your zeal and your mighty acts?
Your tender feeling and your compassion hold themselves back from me.
16Surely you are our Father,
even if Abraham has never heard of us
and Israel would not claim us as his own.
You, LORD, are our Father;
from ages past your name has been Our Redeemer.
17LORD, why do you send us straying from your paths,
and make our hearts so hard that we no longer fear you?
Turn back to us for the sake of your servants,
the tribes that belong to you.
18Your holy people held the land only a short time;
now our enemies have trampled your sanctuary.
19–64:1For a long time now we have been like a people never under your rule,
a people that never bore your name.
If only you would split the heavens apart and come down,
and the mountains would shake as you came near!
fields.summary: One comes from Edom with garments stained from treading the winepress of judgment. The people remember God’s loyal love in the days of Moses and plead for God to return.

fields.title: Isaiah 64
fields.body_html:
Come down, our Father and potter

2Come down like fire that sets dry brush alight, like fire that brings water to the boil;
make your name known to your foes,
and let the nations tremble before you.
3When you did fearsome things beyond all we had hoped,
you came down,
and the mountains shook before you.
4Never since time began has anyone heard of it or taken it in;
no eye has ever seen a God other than you,
one who works for those who wait for him.
5You go out to meet the one who delights in doing righteousness,
those who keep you in mind as they walk in your ways.
But you were angry, and we sinned.
We have stayed in our sins so long; can we be saved?
6We have all turned into something unclean;
our righteous deeds, every one, are like a cloth soiled by a woman’s monthly blood.
We fade like leaves, all of us,
and our guilt carries us off like the wind.
7Not one of us calls on your name;
no one stirs to hold on to you.
For you have hidden your face from us
and let us melt away in the grip of our guilt.
8But now, LORD, you are our Father.
We are the clay, and you the potter who shaped us;
every one of us is what your hand has made.
9LORD, do not let your anger go too far,
and do not keep our guilt in mind forever.
Look at us, we beg you: all of us are your people.
10Your holy cities have turned into open wilderness.
Zion is now a wilderness; Jerusalem lies desolate.
11Our holy and splendid house, where our ancestors once praised you,
has been given to the fire,
and every precious thing we had is now rubble.
12With all this before you, LORD, will you still hold yourself back?
Will you keep silent and afflict us so severely?
fields.summary: The people ask God to tear open the heavens and come down, confessing that even their righteous deeds are like a soiled cloth. God is their father and they are the clay.

fields.title: Isaiah 65
fields.body_html:
Found by those who did not seek

1I made myself available to those who did not ask;
I let myself be found by people who were not looking for me.
“Here I am, here I am,” I said
to a nation that did not bear my name.
2The whole day through I stretched out my hands to a defiant people,
who go along a road that is no good,
wherever their own plans lead them,
3a people who are always angering me, right before my face;
they sacrifice in gardens
and burn incense on bricks,
4who sit among the tombs
and spend the night in hidden spots,
who eat the meat of pigs,
with a stew of foul meat in their pots,
5who say, “Keep your distance;
do not come close to me, for I am holier than you.”
These people are smoke in my nose,
a fire that burns on all day long.
6Look, it is on record before me.
I will not stay silent; instead I will repay,
repaying them straight into their laps,
7for your guilt and the guilt of your ancestors as well, says the LORD.
They made offerings smoke on the mountains
and mocked me on the hills,
so I will measure out what their past deeds have earned and pour it into their laps.

The blessing in the cluster

8The LORD says this: As long as new wine can be found in a bunch of grapes,
people say, “Leave it whole, for there is blessing in it.”
I will do the same for my servants’ sake:
I will not destroy everything.
9From Jacob I will bring out a line of descendants,
and from Judah people to inherit my mountains.
My chosen ones will take possession of it, and my servants will make their home there.
10The plain of Sharon will become grazing land for sheep and goats,
and the Valley of Achor a place where herds lie down,
for my people who have sought me.
11But you who turn away from the LORD,
who have forgotten my holy mountain,
who lay a table for Gad
and fill cups of mixed wine for Meni,
12I will mark you out for the sword, and all of you will kneel down to be slaughtered.
When I called, you gave no answer;
when I spoke, you paid no attention.
You did what is evil in my sight
and chose the very things I take no pleasure in.

Joy for God’s servants in a new creation

13So the Lord GOD says this: See, my servants will eat while you go hungry.
See, my servants will drink while you are thirsty.
See, my servants will be glad while you hang your heads in shame.
14See, my servants will sing out from hearts full of gladness,
but you will cry out from hearts full of pain
and wail because your spirits are crushed.
15Your name will live on only as a curse on the lips of my chosen ones,
and the Lord GOD will put you to death;
but he will call his servants by a different name,
16so that anyone in the land who prays for blessing will pray by the God of Amen,
and anyone in the land who swears an oath will swear it by the God of Amen.
The old troubles will be forgotten;
they will be hidden from my sight.
17Look, I am about to create new heavens and a new earth.
The things of the past will not be remembered;
no one will even think of them again.
18Instead, be joyful and celebrate for all time over what I am creating.
For look, I am creating Jerusalem to be pure gladness, and its people to be pure joy.
19I will be glad over Jerusalem and delight in my people.
No sound of weeping, no cry for help, will be heard in it again.
20There will be no more babies there who live just a few days,
and no old people who fail to complete their years.
Someone who dies at 100 will die as a youth,
and one who falls short of 100 will be held to be under a curse.
21They will build houses and settle in them,
plant vineyards and enjoy their grapes.
22They will not build for others to live in,
or plant for others to eat.
The lifetime of my people will be like the lifetime of a tree,
and my chosen ones will use the work of their own hands to the very end.
23Their work will not be wasted,
nor will they bring children into the world for sudden ruin;
for they are the offspring of those the LORD has blessed,
and their own children with them.
24It will happen that I answer them before they call,
and hear them while the words are still on their lips.
25Wolf and lamb will graze side by side, the lion will eat straw as the ox does,
and the snake will live on dust.
None will hurt and none will destroy anywhere on my holy mountain, says the LORD.
fields.summary: God answers that a rebellious people have been held out to all day long, yet God will spare a faithful remnant. God will create new heavens and a new earth, where the wolf and the lamb will feed together.

fields.title: Isaiah 66
fields.body_html:
Heaven is God’s throne

1The LORD says this: The heavens are my throne,
and the earth is a stool for my feet.
What kind of house would you build for me,
and what kind of place could be my resting place?
2My own hand made all these things,
and that is how they all exist, declares the LORD.
The one I will regard with favor is the lowly, the broken in spirit,
who trembles at my word.
3Slaughtering an ox is no different from killing a person;
sacrificing a lamb, from breaking a dog’s neck;
presenting a grain offering, from offering pig’s blood;
burning frankincense as a memorial, from blessing an idol.
These people have chosen their own ways,
and their hearts delight in their loathsome things.
4So I in turn will choose how harshly to deal with them and will bring on them the very things they fear.
For when I called, no one replied;
when I spoke, they would not listen.
They did what was evil in my sight
and chose what gives me no pleasure.

Zion’s children born in a day

5Hear the word of the LORD,
you who tremble at his word:
Your own kin, who hate you and cast you out because of my name, have said, “Let the LORD show his glory,
and we will see how glad you are!” But it is they who will be put to shame.
6Hear that roar from the city!
Hear the noise from the temple!
It is the sound of the LORD paying back his enemies what they have earned.
7Before her labor began, she gave birth;
before the pangs came over her, she brought a son into the world.
8Who ever heard of anything like this? Who has seen the like?
Is a country brought to birth in a single day,
or a nation born in one moment?
Yet Zion had barely begun her labor when she bore her children.
9Would I bring on the birth and then not let the child be born? says the LORD.
Would I, who bring children to birth, then hold them back? says your God.

10Celebrate with Jerusalem and be glad over her, all who love her.
Join in her great joy, all who have grieved for her,
11so that you may feed at her breast and find comfort and be full,
and draw your fill and revel in her rich glory.

Comfort for Zion and the gathering of the nations

12For the LORD says this: Look, I will make peace flow to her like a river,
and the wealth of the nations like a stream in flood. You will feed at her breast;
she will carry you at her side
and play with you on her knees.
13Just as a mother comforts her own,
so I myself will comfort you;
in Jerusalem you will be comforted.
14You will see this and your hearts will be glad;
your bones will spring up like new grass.
It will be known that the hand of the LORD is with his servants,
but he will be furious with his enemies.
15Look! the LORD comes in fire,
and his chariots sweep in like a storm,
to give vent to his anger in fury
and his rebuke in tongues of fire.
16By fire and by his sword the LORD will bring all humanity to judgment,
and those struck down by the LORD will be many.
17Those who set themselves apart and cleanse themselves to enter the gardens, following the one in the center,
who eat pork, vile creatures and mice,
will perish together, declares the LORD.
18I, for my part, know their deeds and their schemes. The time is coming for gathering every nation and language, and they will come and look on my glory. 19I will put a sign among them. From them I will send survivors out to the nations: to Tarshish, to Pul and to Lud, the people who draw the bow, to Tubal and Javan, and to the far coastlands that have not heard the news of me or seen my glory. They will tell of my glory among the nations. 20They will bring all your kin out of every nation as an offering to the LORD. They will come on horses, in chariots and covered carts, on mules and on swift camels, to my holy mountain, Jerusalem, says the LORD, as the Israelites bring grain offerings to the house of the LORD in clean vessels. 21And I will even take some of them to be priests and Levites, says the LORD.
22The new heavens and the new earth that I am about to make will stand firm in my presence, declares the LORD;
in the same way your descendants and your name will stand firm.
23Month after month at the new moon,
and week after week on the Sabbath,
all humanity will come to bow in worship before me, says the LORD.
24Then they will go out and gaze on the corpses of the people who rebelled against me.
For their worm will not die, nor will their fire be put out,
and they will be a horror to every living being.
fields.summary: Heaven is God’s throne and earth God’s footstool, and God looks to the humble. Jerusalem will rejoice like a mother with her children, and all people will come to worship God.

fields.title: Conclusion
fields.body_html:
The new heavens and the new earth that I am about to make will stand firm in my presence, declares the LORD; in the same way your descendants and your name will stand firm.

— Isaiah 66:22

Isaiah began with a rebellious people and a land in ruins. It ends with new heavens and a new earth, and with a promise that God’s people, and their name, will stand as firm as the new creation itself. Between the two lie the throne room and the burning coal, the child and the shoot from Jesse’s stump, the highway in the wilderness, the servant pierced for others, and a feast for all the peoples on the mountain of the LORD.

But Isaiah is honest to the very end. Its last verse looks at those who rebelled and would not come. The book will not let its readers forget that the Holy One of Israel is holy, or that his invitation can be refused.

The question the book leaves with you

Two questions in Isaiah stay with the reader long after the last page. The first is the one Isaiah heard in the temple: “Whom am I to send? Who will go on our behalf?” (6:8). The second is the question that opens the song of the suffering servant:

Who has believed the news that reached us? And the arm of the LORD, to whom has it been laid bare?

— Isaiah 53:1

The good news that reached Israel was strange news: that God would save the world through a servant who was despised and rejected, who had “no fine looks to make us long for him”, and whose death would bring healing to those who had turned their faces away. Paul quotes this question when he writes about those who had heard the gospel and not believed (Romans 10:16). Isaiah asks it of everyone who reads him. The book is full of invitations — “Come, let us take this matter to court together”, “Listen, all who thirst: come down to the water!”, “Turn toward me and be saved” — and each of them waits for an answer. “Look for the LORD while he can still be found; call to him while he is close by” (55:6).

Where Isaiah points

The New Testament reads Isaiah as a book about Jesus. The Gospels open with Isaiah’s voice in the wilderness, and Matthew with Isaiah’s child called Immanuel. Jesus reads Isaiah 61 in the synagogue and says it has come true. Matthew finds the gentle servant of chapter 42 in Jesus’s healing; Philip finds Jesus in chapter 53; Paul hears the good news of chapter 52 in every messenger of the gospel. John goes further still: after quoting Isaiah 6, he writes, “Isaiah said these things because he saw his glory and spoke about him” (John 12:41). The King on the high throne was the one who would be lifted up on a cross.

And the last book of the Bible ends with Isaiah’s last vision: “Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth” (Revelation 21:1). The one on the throne says, “See, I am making everything new!” The hope Isaiah saw from afar is the hope the church still waits for.

Where to go from here

Isaiah has been preached, sung and loved by the church in every century, and some of the best of that work is in this library. A few places to begin:

  • On the vision of the Holy One (Isaiah 6). A. W. Tozer’s sermon The Seraphim’s Worship, on 6:1–4.
  • On the texts of Handel’s Messiah. John Newton’s discourses Comfort Ye My People (40:1), Unto Us a Child Is Born (9:6) and Messiah Suffering and Wounded for Us (53:4–5).
  • On the prophecies of Christ. Justin Martyr’s Dialogue with Trypho, the second-century conversation in which Justin argues from Isaiah, among other prophets, that Jesus is the Christ, with chapters on Isaiah 7:14.
  • On the gentle servant (Isaiah 42:1–3). Richard Sibbes’s The Bruised Reed, on the reed he will not snap and the wick he will not smother, as Matthew 12 quotes them.
  • On waiting and renewed strength (Isaiah 40). Alexander Maclaren’s The Secret of Immortal Youth (40:30–31), and Andrew Murray’s Waiting on God, which takes several of its thirty-one days from Isaiah (8:17; 25:9; 30:18; 40:31; 64:4).
  • On God’s care for his people. Charles H. Spurgeon’s Fear Not (41:14) and Maclaren’s The Writing on God’s Hands (49:16).
  • On the great invitation (Isaiah 55). Maclaren’s The Call to the Thirsty.
  • On the Spirit in Isaiah. The chapter “The Holy Spirit in the Book of Isaiah” in A. B. Simpson’s The Holy Spirit, or Power from on High, Part I, which traces the Spirit from Isaiah’s own consecration to the Spirit resting on the promised Christ, on Israel and on each believer.
  • On Hezekiah’s prayer (Isaiah 37). The Prayers Jesus Learned, an Ochorus Original, whose chapter “Opening the Letter Before the Lord” follows the king who spread the Assyrian letter before God, as 2 Kings 19 tells it.

You can also go the other way, from the text to the classics. Every reference to Isaiah in this library can be tapped to read the verse, and the Scripture pages gather, chapter by chapter, what the great writers of the church have said about each passage of this book.

Isaiah is long, and no one takes it in on a first reading. But it rewards every return, and it makes a promise about itself that the centuries have kept:

Just as rain and snow fall from the heavens and do not go back up until they have soaked the ground and made it bud and grow, giving seed to the one who sows and bread to the one who eats, so it is with the word that leaves my mouth: it will not come back to me with nothing done, but it will do what I want and succeed in the errand I sent it on.

— Isaiah 55:10–11
